output.prompt: Imagine you missed an important call from a friend because you had already gone out. Write a short message (3-5 sentences) to your friend to apologize and explain what happened. Make sure to use the past perfect tense.
output.cn: 想象你错过了一个朋友的重要电话，因为你已经外出了。给你的朋友写一个短消息（3-5句），道歉并解释发生了什么。确保使用过去完成时。

reading.cn: 梅的早晨很忙碌。她的寄宿家庭妈妈琳达在上午9点给她打了电话，但是梅没有接。那是因为梅已经出门去图书馆了。中午梅回到家时，她看到了琳达的未接电话。梅立刻给琳达回电道歉。“琳达，真抱歉！你打电话来的时候我已经出门了，”梅解释说。琳达说：“没关系，梅。我只是想问你是否记得锁前门了。”梅检查后确认：“是的，我出门前就已经锁好了。”
reading.en: Mei had a busy morning. Her host mom, Linda, called her at 9 AM, but Mei didn't answer. That's because Mei had already left the house to go to the library. When Mei returned home at noon, she saw a missed call from Linda. Mei immediately called Linda back to apologize. "I'm so sorry, Linda! I had already left when you called," Mei explained. Linda said, "No problem, Mei. I just wanted to ask if you had remembered to lock the front door." Mei checked and confirmed, "Yes, I had locked it before I left."

reading.cn: 琳达接着问：“那你出门前已经吃过早餐了吗？”梅笑了：“是的，我吃了一顿丰盛的早餐！”琳达笑了，“好！我只是想确保你出门前把所有事情都做好了。下次，如果你已经出门了或者正要出门，给我发个快速信息就行。”
reading.en: Linda then asked, "And had you already eaten breakfast before you left?" Mei laughed, "Yes, I had eaten a big breakfast!" Linda smiled, "Good! I just wanted to make sure you had everything covered before you headed out. Next time, just send me a quick text if you've already left or are about to leave."

reading.cn: 梅觉得松了口气。她很高兴自己道了歉并澄清了情况。她还决定将来更注意查看手机并告知琳达。梅心想：“让琳达知道很重要，尤其她这么体贴。”
reading.en: Mei felt relieved. She was glad she had apologized and clarified the situation. She also decided to be more mindful of checking her phone and informing Linda in the future. Mei thought, "It's important to keep Linda informed, especially since she's so thoughtful."

reading.cn: 那天晚上晚些时候，梅接到了琳达的另一个电话。这次，梅很快接了电话。琳达说：“嗨，梅！我只是想确认我们明天的晚餐计划。你已经做了其他计划了吗？”梅回答说：“不，我没有做任何其他计划。我有空！”琳达很高兴。“太棒了！我买了食材了，”她说。梅很高兴她接了电话。
reading.en: Later that evening, Mei received another call from Linda. This time, Mei answered quickly. Linda said, "Hi Mei! I just wanted to confirm our dinner plans for tomorrow. Had you already made other plans?" Mei replied, "No, I hadn't made any other plans. I'm free!" Linda was happy. "Great! I've already bought the ingredients," she said. Mei was glad she had answered the phone.

grammar.title: 过去完成时 (Past Perfect)
grammar.explain: 过去完成时表示在过去某个时间点或动作之前已经完成的动作或状态。它通常用于强调动作的先后顺序，即“在...之前”已经发生的事情。其构成是 'had + 动词的过去分词 (past participle)'。

examples.cn: 她说她已经决定了。（“决定”发生在“说”之前）
examples.en: She said she had already decided.

examples.cn: 他到的时候，我已经完成工作了。（“完成工作”发生在“他到”之前）
examples.en: I had already finished my work when he arrived.
They had lived in Beijing for five years before they moved to Shanghai.
examples.cn: 在他们搬到上海之前，他们已经在北京住了五年。（“住在北京”发生在“搬到上海”之前）

examples.en: Wei had hesitated to tell anyone until all the arrangements were firm.
examples.cn: 在所有安排确定之前，薇一直犹豫着没有告诉任何人。（“犹豫”发生在“告诉”之前，且在故事主线叙述之前）

examples.en: She had never been so excited.
examples.cn: 她从未如此兴奋过。（“从未如此兴奋”是在那个特定时间点前的状态）
我早觉得一切都会顺利的。（“感觉”发生在“事情顺利进行”之前）
examples.en: I had a feeling it would all work out.

grammar.title: 过去完成时在叙事中的应用
grammar.explain: 当我们在讲述一个过去的故事时，如果提到一个比故事主线更早发生的事件，通常会使用过去完成时。这有助于读者或听者理解事件发生的时间顺序。

reading.en: Wei and her best friend, Lily, were having coffee. Lily was excited to share news about an exchange program. “Lily, I have something to tell you,” Wei said, taking a sip of her latte. “I'm going to high school in the U.S.!” Lily was surprised. “What? When did you decide this?” Wei smiled, “I had already decided last month. My parents and I had talked about it for a long time. They had found a great school in California, and we had completed all the applications. Everything was already arranged.” Lily felt a little sad because she would miss Wei, but also very happy for her. “That’s amazing! Why didn’t you tell me sooner?” Wei explained, “I wanted to be sure everything was set before I shared the big news. I had hesitated to tell anyone until all the arrangements were firm. But now, it’s really happening!”
reading.cn: 薇和她的好朋友莉莉正在喝咖啡。莉莉很兴奋地想分享一个交换项目的消息。“莉莉，我有些事情要告诉你，” 薇喝了一口拿铁说，“我要去美国读高中了！” 莉莉很惊讶。“什么？你什么时候决定的？” 薇笑着说，“我上个月就已经决定了。我父母和我已经谈论了很长时间。他们已经在加利福尼亚找到了一所很棒的学校，并且我们已经完成了所有的申请。一切都已经安排好了。” 莉莉有点难过，因为她会想念薇，但也为她感到非常高兴。“太棒了！你为什么不早点告诉我？” 薇解释说，“我想在一切都确定之后再分享这个大消息。在所有安排确定之前，我一直犹豫着没有告诉任何人。但现在，它真的要发生了！”

reading.en: Lily raised her cup. “Well, congratulations on your big adventure! I'm going to miss you, but I know this is a wonderful opportunity. What about your English? Have you been practicing?” Wei nodded, “Yes, I had already started extra English classes a few months ago. I also had watched many American TV shows to get used to the accent. I feel ready!” They spent the rest of their afternoon dreaming about Wei’s future in the U.S. high school.
reading.cn: 莉莉举起杯子。“好吧，祝贺你的大冒险！我会想你的，但我知道这是一个绝佳的机会。你的英语怎么样？你一直在练习吗？” 薇点点头说，“是的，我几个月前就已经开始上额外的英语课了。我还看了很多美国电视节目来适应口音。我觉得我准备好了！” 她们度过了一个下午，梦想着薇在美国高中学习的未来。
当薇回到家时，她的父母告诉她学校已经发来了最终确认函。她的入学手续已经完成了！她从未如此兴奋过。这是一个梦想成真，一个她已经秘密地培养了多年的梦想。
reading.en: When Wei arrived home, her parents told her that the school had sent the final confirmation. Her enrollment was complete! She had never been so excited. This was a dream come true, a dream she had secretly nurtured for years.

reading.cn: 第二天，薇给莉莉打电话。“莉莉，你猜怎么着？学校发来了最终确认函！我的入学手续已经完成了。” 莉莉高兴地尖叫起来。“太棒了！我早觉得一切都会顺利的。”
reading.en: The next day, Wei called Lily. “Guess what, Lily? The school sent the final confirmation! My enrollment is complete.” Lily shrieked with joy. “That’s fantastic! I had a feeling it would all work out.”

reading.cn: 梅在公共休息室看到安娜看起来很难过。“怎么了，安娜？”梅问道。安娜叹了口气。“我刚收到一封邮件。我的大学申请被拒了。”梅的眼睛睁大了。“哦不，我很抱歉听到这个消息！是哪所大学？”安娜解释说，她申请了英国一所大学的奖学金项目。“我真的很想去，”她说着，声音渐渐低了下去。梅感到一阵后悔。“安娜，你为什么不告诉我？如果我早知道，我一定会帮你！我之前经历过那个申请过程。我本可以帮你审阅你的论文或者帮助你进行面试的。”安娜耸了耸肩。“我不想打扰你。你看起来很忙。”梅摇了摇头。“不，安娜，永远不要犹豫寻求帮助。我们是朋友。我真的很后悔没有早点知道这件事。那是一个很好的机会。”安娜虚弱地笑了笑。“谢谢你，梅。知道你会支持我，这对我意义重大。”梅把手放在她的肩膀上。“当然。让我们寻找一些其他的机会。我们可以一起找。”
reading.en: Mei found Anna looking sad in the common room. "What's wrong, Anna?" Mei asked. Anna sighed. "I just got an email. My university application was rejected." Mei's eyes widened. "Oh no, I'm so sorry to hear that! Which university was it?" Anna explained that she'd applied for a scholarship program at a university in the UK. "I really wanted to go," she said, her voice trailing off. Mei felt a pang of regret. "Anna, why didn't you tell me? If I had known, I would have helped you! I've been through that application process before. I could have looked over your essays or helped you with the interview." Anna shrugged. "I didn't want to bother you. You seemed so busy." Mei shook her head. "No, Anna, never hesitate to ask for help. We're friends. I really regret not knowing about this sooner. It was a great opportunity." Anna smiled weakly. "Thanks, Mei. It means a lot to know you'd support me." Mei put a hand on her shoulder. "Of course. Let's find some other opportunities. We can look together."

Mei felt a pang of regret and thought, "If only I had known about Anna's application earlier! I wish I had asked her if she needed any help. I could have shared my experience with her." Anna, too, had a moment of reflection. "If I hadn't been so hesitant, I would have asked Mei for her advice. Maybe things would have been different." Looking at Mei's genuine concern, Anna felt a little better. "It's okay, Mei. What's done is done. We can't change the past, but we can learn from it." Mei nodded, "Exactly. Next time, let's keep each other in the loop." They both silently agreed to communicate more openly in the future.
reading.cn: 梅感到一阵后悔，心想：“要是我早知道安娜的申请就好了！我希望我当时问过她是否需要任何帮助。我本可以和她分享我的经验的。”安娜也有一刻的反思。“要是我当时没有那么犹豫，我就会向梅寻求建议了。也许事情就会不同了。”看着梅真诚的关心，安娜感觉好些了。“没关系，梅。木已成舟。我们无法改变过去，但我们可以从中学习。”梅点点头，“没错。下次，我们互相保持联系。”她们俩都默默同意以后要更公开地交流。

reading.en: Mei understood that sometimes people don't ask for help because they don't want to be a burden. "Anna, I know it's hard to ask for help sometimes, but friends are here for that. If you ever feel overwhelmed or unsure about something, please tell me. We are a team, right?" Anna smiled warmly. "Right. And Mei, if something is bothering you, you should also tell me. I want to be there for you too." Their shared experience, though born from a disappointment, strengthened their friendship.
reading.cn: 梅明白，有时人们不寻求帮助是因为他们不想成为负担。“安娜，我知道有时寻求帮助很难，但朋友就是为此而存在的。如果你感到不知所措或对某事不确定，请告诉我。我们是一个团队，对吗？”安娜温暖地笑了。“对。还有梅，如果有什么事困扰你，你也要告诉我。我也想为你分忧。”她们共同的经历，虽然源于一次失望，却加深了她们的友谊。

reading.en: Later that week, Mei remembered something her high school counselor often said: "It's better to regret something you did than something you didn't do." She shared this with Anna. "See, Anna, even if we tried and failed, at least we wouldn't have the 'if only I had...' feeling." Anna nodded thoughtfully. "You're right. I should have been more proactive. But now I know for next time. And thank you for reminding me that it's okay to ask for help." Mei smiled, glad that something positive could come out of the situation. They made a plan to research other scholarship opportunities together.
reading.cn: 那周晚些时候，梅想起她的高中辅导员经常说的一句话：“做了后悔好过没做后悔。”她把这句话告诉了安娜。“你看，安娜，即使我们尝试了并且失败了，至少我们也不会有‘要是我当时……’的感觉了。”安娜若有所思地点点头。“你说得对。我当时应该更积极主动一些。但现在我知道下次该怎么做了。谢谢你提醒我寻求帮助没关系。”梅笑了，很高兴这件事能带来一些积极的结果。她们计划一起研究其他奖学金机会。

reading.cn: 梅和安娜做室友几个月了。最近，梅觉得安娜对她有点疏远。她经常看到安娜很晚回家，然后在电话里低声说话。梅以为安娜是故意躲着她，甚至怀疑安娜在没告诉她的情况下找新室友。一个晚上，梅最终和安娜对质了。“安娜，我觉得你一直在躲着我。如果你想找新室友，你早该告诉我！”梅脱口而出，声音充满了失望。安娜看起来很惊讶。“梅，你在说什么？我没有躲着你。我只是想保守一个秘密，因为我正在为你准备一个惊喜生日派对！所有那些熬夜和低语都是为了和我们的朋友协调。我很抱歉，我不是故意让你难过的。”梅感到一阵轻松和 L 尬。“哦，安娜！我也很抱歉。我完全误解了。我妄下结论了。我早该问你的，而不是想当然。”安娜笑了。“没关系，梅。沟通是关键。我们现在已经解决了。”她们拥抱了一下，误会终于解除了，这让她们的友谊更加坚固了。
reading.en: Mei and Anna had been roommates for a few months. Lately, Mei felt a bit distant from Anna. She often saw Anna coming home late and whispering on the phone. Mei thought Anna was intentionally avoiding her and even suspected Anna was looking for a new roommate without telling her. One evening, Mei finally confronted Anna. "Anna, I feel like you've been avoiding me. And you should have told me sooner if you wanted a new roommate!" Mei blurted out, her voice filled with disappointment. Anna looked surprised. "Mei, what are you talking about? I haven't been avoiding you. I was just trying to keep a secret because I was planning a surprise birthday party for you! All the late nights and whispering were about coordinating with our friends. I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to make you feel bad." Mei felt a wave of relief and embarrassment. "Oh, Anna! I'm so sorry too. I completely misunderstood. I jumped to conclusions. I should have asked you earlier instead of assuming things." Anna smiled. "It's okay, Mei. Communication is key. We've resolved it now." They hugged, and the misunderstanding was finally cleared up, making their friendship even stronger.

grammar.title: 让步连接词: Though / Although / Even though

grammar.explain:
这些连接词用于引出让步状语从句，表示与主句内容相反或出乎意料的情况。它们的意思相近，都表示“尽管”、“虽然”。

- **Though**：可以用于句首、句中或句尾，相对口语化。
- **Although**：通常用于句首，语气比 though 稍正式。
- **Even though**：语气最强，强调“即使”或“尽管如此”的意思。

**核心句型示例：**
Though she had little hope, Sue never gave up trying to encourage Johnsy.

grammar.title: 过去完成时 (Past Perfect)
grammar.explain:
过去完成时表示在过去某个时间点之前已经完成的动作。它常用于叙述故事，表明事件发生的先后顺序。

结构：had + 动词过去分词 (V-ed/V3)

**核心句型示例：**
Johnsy had made up her mind that she was not going to get well.

reading.cn: 那是一个格林威治村寒冷的十一月。苏和琼西，两位年轻艺术家，共用一间位于三层砖楼顶层的画室公寓。琼西患上了肺炎，医生几乎没有给她希望。医生告诉苏：“她只有十分之一的机会，这个机会取决于她是否愿意活下去。你的这位年轻女士已经下定决心，她不会好起来了。”琼西躺在床上，看着窗外对面砖墙上的一棵老常春藤。秋天冰冷的风已经吹走了它大部分叶子。“当最后一片叶子落下时，”琼西低声说，“我也必须离开了。”
reading.en: It was a cold November in Greenwich Village. Sue and Johnsy, two young artists, shared a studio apartment at the top of a three-story brick building. Johnsy had fallen ill with pneumonia, and the doctor had given her little hope. He told Sue, "She has one chance in ten, and that chance is for her to want to live. Your little lady has made up her mind that she's not going to get well." Johnsy lay in bed, looking out the window at an old ivy vine on the opposite brick wall. The cold breath of autumn had blown most of its leaves away. "When the last leaf falls," Johnsy whispered, "I must go, too."

listening.audio: Mei and Wei are talking about school applications. Mei says, "According to the article, Northwood Academy accepts only 12% of students. It's a very competitive school." Wei replies, "Wow, that's a low admission rate. I hope my application stands out."

reading.cn: 梅正在为她的侄女薇研究高中。她在网上找到一篇关于北木学院的文章，那是一所著名的寄宿学校。“薇，听听这个，”梅边读着平板电脑边说，“报道说，这所学校只录取12%的申请者。竞争非常激烈！”薇叹了口气。“哇，录取率真低。你觉得我有机会吗？”梅笑了笑。“别担心。文章还提到他们看重有力的论文和好的推荐信。我们重点让你的申请脱颖而出。”
reading.en: Mei was researching high schools for her niece, Wei. She found an article online about Northwood Academy, a prestigious boarding school. “Wei, listen to this,” Mei said, reading from her tablet. “According to the article, the school accepts only 12% of applicants. It’s very competitive!” Wei sighed. “Wow, that’s a low admission rate. Do you think I have a chance?” Mei smiled. “Don’t worry. The article also mentions they look for strong essays and good recommendations. Let’s focus on making your application stand out.”

reading.cn: 几周后，薇完成了她的申请。“我寄出去了，梅姨！”她宣布道，既紧张又充满希望。梅抱了抱她，“太棒了！现在我们等着。记住，无论结果如何，你都尽了最大努力。而且总有其他很棒的学校。”薇点点头，期待着收到录取通知书——或者被拒——的那一天，但她觉得她已经为任何一种结果做好了准备。
reading.en: A few weeks later, Wei finished her application. “I sent it in, Aunt Mei!” she announced, feeling nervous but hopeful. Mei hugged her. “That’s fantastic! Now we wait. Remember, no matter the outcome, you’ve put in your best effort. And there are always other great schools.” Wei nodded, looking forward to the day she might receive an acceptance letter – or perhaps a rejection – but she felt ready for either.

reading.cn: 几个月过去了。一天下午，薇收到了封邮件。她颤抖着手打开了它。主题行写着：“北木学院申请更新。”她深吸一口气。“梅姨，”她喊道，“我需要你在这里。”梅赶紧跑过来。她们一起读了第一行：“恭喜！我们很高兴通知您，您已被北木学院录取。”薇高兴地尖叫起来。“我被录取了！文章说有多难是真的，但我做到了！”梅紧紧抱住侄女。“我就知道你能行。你所有的努力都得到了回报。”
reading.en: Months passed. One afternoon, Wei received an email. Her hands trembled as she opened it. The subject line read: “Northwood Academy Application Update.” She took a deep breath. “Aunt Mei,” she called out, “I need you here.” Mei rushed over. Together, they read the first line: “Congratulations! We are pleased to inform you of your acceptance to Northwood Academy.” Wei shrieked with joy. “I got in! The article was right about how difficult it is, but I did it!” Mei hugged her niece tightly. “I knew you could. All your hard work paid off.”

reading.cn: 梅接着建议道，“既然你被录取了，我们再去看看校园吧。文章里有一些很棒的照片，但亲自去会更好。”薇热情地同意了。她们计划在接下来的周末去参观，渴望探索她未来的学校。
reading.en: Mei then suggested, “Now that you’re accepted, let’s revisit the campus. The article had some great pictures, but it's even better in person.” Wei agreed enthusiastically. They planned a visit the following weekend, eager to explore her future school.

reading.cn: 在薇来美国之前，她的家人开了一个重要的会议。她的父母和哥哥李坐在厨房的桌子旁。“那么，关于去美国的事，”妈妈开口了。薇有点紧张。爸爸补充道，“薇，这是很重要的一步，我们想确保你准备好了。”李点点头。“我们需要讨论所有事情，好的和不好的。”薇深吸一口气。“我知道这是一个重大的决定，”她说。妈妈笑了。“但这是你的梦想，我们支持你。”爸爸接着说，“薇，这个决定是大家一起做的。我们是一家人。”李插话道，“是的，我们需要计划好一切，这样你才能有一个顺利的开始。”薇感到一阵轻松。她知道她的家人是她最大的支持系统。
reading.en: Before Wei came to the U.S., her family had an important meeting. Her parents and her older brother, Li, sat together at the kitchen table. "So, about going to America," her mom started. Wei felt a little nervous. Her dad added, "It's a big step, Wei, and we want to make sure you're ready." Li nodded. "We need to discuss everything, good and bad." Wei took a deep breath. "I know it's a big decision," she said. Her mom smiled. "But it's your dream, and we support you." Her dad continued, "The decision was made together, Wei. We're a family." Li chimed in, "Yes, we need to plan everything so you have a smooth start." Wei felt a wave of relief. She knew her family was her biggest support system.

They talked for hours. They discussed the cost of living, the university programs, and how they would keep in touch. Her parents reminded her that even if things got tough, they were always there for her. Li offered to help her with visa documents and finding an apartment. By the end of the evening, Wei felt incredibly grateful. The family agreed on the plan. This wasn't just *her* decision; it was *their* decision. It was a shared journey, and she felt ready to embrace it.
reading.cn: 他们谈了几个小时。他们讨论了生活费、大学课程以及如何保持联系。她的父母提醒她，即使遇到困难，他们也永远在她身边。李主动提出帮她办理签证文件和找公寓。到了晚上，薇感到无比感激。一家人就计划达成了一致。这不仅仅是她一个人的决定；这是他们大家的决定。这是一趟共同的旅程，她觉得已经准备好去迎接它了。
几周后，当薇即将离开时，爸爸紧紧抱住了她。“记住，”他说，“无论如何，我们都为你骄傲。而这段旅程？这是一个充满爱和支持的家庭选择。”薇知道她不仅承载着自己的梦想，还有全家人的希望和努力。
reading.en: Weeks later, when Wei was about to leave, her dad hugged her tightly. "Remember," he said, "no matter what, we are proud of you. And this journey? It was a family choice, made with love and support." Wei knew she wasn't just carrying her own dreams, but the hopes and efforts of her entire family.
On the plane, Wei looked out the window. The decision was made together. This thought filled her heart with warmth and courage.
reading.cn: 在飞机上，薇看向窗外。这个决定是大家一起做的。这个想法让她的内心充满了温暖和勇气。

grammar.title: 被动语态 (The Passive Voice): The decision was made together.
grammar.explain: 被动语态用于强调动作的承受者而不是动作的发出者。在标题句 "The decision was made together" 中，我们更关注“决定”本身以及它是如何被做出的，而不是谁做了这个决定。常见的被动语态结构是：主语 + be动词 + 过去分词。
动词 discuss 表示“讨论”，后面直接跟讨论的内容，不需要加介词。例如，我们讨论一个计划，就用 discuss a plan，而不需要 discuss about a plan。

examples.cn: 我们讨论这个项目讨论了两个小时。

reading.en: Mei was talking to her mom about a new work project. Mei’s mom thought Mei should take a very traditional approach, but Mei had a different idea. “I think we should try a new marketing strategy, Mom,” Mei said. Her mom replied, “Oh, Mei, I’m not so sure about that. The old ways always work best.” Mei smiled. “I understand your point, but I really believe this new approach could bring better results.” Her mom nodded slowly. “Well, I suppose it’s worth a try. Just make sure to be careful.” Mei was happy they could discuss it respectfully.

reading.en: Later that day, Mei was having a discussion with her colleague, Tom, about the same project. Tom suggested a very risky idea. Mei listened carefully, then said, “That’s an interesting suggestion, Tom, but I’m not so sure about that. It seems a bit too risky for us right now.” Tom appreciated her honesty. “You have a point,” he admitted. “Maybe we can find a compromise.” They continued to talk, considering different perspectives to find the best solution.

reading.en: Mei learned that day that disagreeing respectfully is an important skill in both family and work life.

reading.en: Mei was preparing for her annual performance review. Her manager, Mr. Smith, had asked her to come prepared to discuss her achievements and challenges from the past year. Mei carefully reviewed her notes, recalling key projects and the various incidents that had occurred. She had worked on the new marketing campaign, which was very successful. However, there was one difficult client interaction she also needed to mention. As she was going through her memories, she realized the importance of narrating these events clearly and accurately, using different tenses to show the sequence of her actions and their consequences. She wanted to present a complete and chronological timeline of her contributions.

grammar.title: 叙事时态混搭 (Narrative Tense Blending)
grammar.explain:
在讲述过去发生的故事或经历时，我们经常会混用不同的过去时态，以清晰地表达事件发生的顺序、背景和持续性。

**核心句型一：一般过去时 (Simple Past) - 描述主要动作或事件。**

**核心句型二：过去进行时 (Past Continuous) - 描述过去某个时间点正在进行或作为背景的动作。**

**核心句型三：过去完成时 (Past Perfect) - 描述在另一个过去动作之前已经完成的动作。**

examples.cn: 我当时正在写报告，这时客户打来了电话。

reading.en: Breaking news! Mei walks into the living room where Mr. and Mrs. Walker are reading. She has a big smile on her face. "I have some exciting news to announce!" she says, her voice full of joy. Mr. Walker lowers his newspaper. "Oh? What is it, Mei?" Mrs. Walker asks, curiosity in her eyes. "I chose Riverside! I got accepted, and I decided to go there," Mei announces, almost jumping with excitement. Mr. Walker beams. "That's wonderful, Mei! We're so proud of you." Mrs. Walker adds, "Riverside is a fantastic school. We know you'll do great things there." Mei admits, "I was a little nervous about making the decision, but I feel good about it now. It's a big opportunity." They all share a moment of happiness, celebrating Mei's new adventure.

reading.cn: 梅已经向 Riverside 大学发出了接受通知，这是她经过认真考虑后做出的决定。她期待着秋季开始她的课程。Walker 一家非常支持她，并提出会在她需要的时候提供帮助，从购买新教材到熟悉校园生活。梅非常感谢他们的帮助，迫不及待地想开启这一新篇章。
reading.en: Mei has already sent her acceptance to Riverside University, a decision she made after careful consideration. She's looking forward to starting her classes in the fall. The Walkers are very supportive and have offered to help her with anything she needs, from buying new textbooks to navigating campus life. Mei is grateful for their help and can't wait to begin this new chapter.

reading.cn: 梅的决定并非易事。她有几个选择，但 Riverside 为她的专业提供了最好的课程。它还有一个美丽的校园，有很多学生活动。她相信这个机会将帮助她在学业和个人方面都取得成长。
reading.en: Mei's decision wasn't easy. She had a few options, but Riverside offered the best program for her major. It also has a beautiful campus with many student activities. She believes this opportunity will help her grow both academically and personally.

grammar.explain: 本课标题“What a moment!”是一个感叹句，用来表达强烈的情感，如惊喜、高兴、赞美等。感叹句的常见形式有两种：以What开头和以How开头。

output.prompt: Imagine you are Mei. Write a short journal entry about your feelings and what happened when you picked up Wei at the airport today.
output.cn: 想象你是梅。写一篇短日志，记录你今天在机场接到薇薇时的感受和发生的事情。
output.sample: Today was truly special! I finally picked up Wei at SFO. My heart was racing when I saw her. We shared the biggest hug! It was such an exciting moment. I'm so happy she's here in San Francisco.

reading.en: Mei felt a rush of excitement as her taxi pulled up to the arrivals area at San Francisco International Airport (SFO). She had been looking forward to this day for months. Her best friend, Wei, was finally arriving from China. Mei checked the flight status one last time on her phone. “Flight CA985, arrived,” the screen proudly displayed. Her heart beat a little faster. She quickly walked into the terminal, scanning the faces in the crowd. And then she saw her! Wei, with a big suitcase and an even bigger smile. “Wei!” Mei cried out, tears welling up in her eyes. Wei dropped her bags and rushed to Mei. They shared a long, warm hug. “What a moment!” Mei whispered, holding her friend tightly. “Welcome to San Francisco!”
reading.cn: 梅的士驶入旧金山国际机场 (SFO) 的到达区时，她感到一阵激动。她盼望这一天已经好几个月了。她最好的朋友薇薇终于要从中国来了。梅最后一次在手机上查看航班状态。“航班 CA985，已抵达，”屏幕上自豪地显示着。她的心跳得更快了。她快步走进航站楼，扫视着人群中的面孔。然后她看到了她！薇薇，带着一个大行李箱，笑容更灿烂了。“薇薇！”梅喊道，眼泪涌了出来。薇薇放下行李，冲向梅。她们紧紧地拥抱。“多么珍贵的时刻啊！”梅紧紧地抱着朋友，低声说。“欢迎来到旧金山！”
薇薇笑了，那是梅很久没有亲耳听到的声音。“见到你真好，梅！航班很长，但很值得。”梅退后一步，仍然牵着薇薇的手。“走吧，我们去拿你的行李，然后我们就可以回家了。我为你计划了好多要看要玩的东西！”薇薇点点头，眼睛里闪烁着期待。取完行李后，她们走出机场，兴奋地聊着天。旧金山的空气清新凉爽。梅止不住地微笑。薇薇终于在这里了，这让一切都感觉完整。这确实是一个她会永远珍藏的时刻。
reading.en: Wei laughed, a sound Mei hadn't heard in person for too long. “It’s so good to see you, Mei! The flight was long, but it was worth it.” Mei stepped back, still holding Wei's hands. “Come on, let’s get your luggage and then we can head home. I’ve planned so many things for you to see and do!” Wei nodded, her eyes shining with anticipation. After collecting the luggage, they walked out of the airport, chatting excitedly. The San Francisco air felt fresh and cool. Mei couldn't stop smiling. Having Wei here, finally, made everything feel complete. This was indeed a moment she would cherish forever.
Mei said, “What a beautiful day to welcome you!” Wei replied, “Yes, I'm so happy to be here!”
reading.cn: 梅说：“多美好的一天来欢迎你啊！” 薇薇回答：“是啊，我真高兴来到这里！”

reading.en: Later, on the drive home, Wei looked out the window. “Everything is so new and different,” she commented. “I can’t wait to explore more!” Mei smiled. “Don't worry, we have plenty of time. This is just the beginning of your amazing adventure!” Wei agreed, feeling a warmth spread through her. Being reunited with Mei, in a new country, felt like the start of something truly special. “What a moment,” she thought to herself, echoing Mei's earlier words. “What a truly wonderful moment.”
reading.cn: 后来，在回家的路上，薇薇看着窗外。“一切都那么新奇和不同，”她评论道。“我迫不及待地想探索更多！”梅笑了。“别担心，我们有充足的时间。这只是你美妙冒险的开始！”薇薇同意了，感到一股暖流传遍全身。在新国家与梅团聚，感觉就像是真正特别的事情的开始。“多么珍贵的时刻啊，”她心里想着，回应着梅之前的话。“多么真正美妙的时刻。”

output.prompt:
You need to write a formal email to a university to inquire about their scholarship application process. You don't know the exact person to address. Write a short email (3-5 sentences) covering:
1.  Formal salutation.
2.  Your purpose for writing (to inquire about scholarships).

output.cn:
你需要给一所大学写一封正式邮件，询问他们的奖学金申请流程。你不知道具体的收件人是谁。写一封简短的邮件（3-5句话），包含：
1.  正式称谓。

output.sample:

I am writing to inquire about the scholarship application process for prospective students. Could you please provide information on the eligibility criteria and the application deadline for the upcoming academic year? Your guidance on this matter would be greatly appreciated. Thank you for your time and consideration.

grammar.title: Formal Salutations: To Whom It May Concern
grammar.explain: 在正式的商务信函或电子邮件中，当你不知道具体收件人的名字或职位时，可以使用“To Whom It May Concern.”。这是一种非常正式且广泛接受的称谓，表示你的信件是写给任何负责处理你所提及事项的人。

examples.cn: 致相关负责人：我写信是为了询问一个职位空缺。

examples.en: To Whom It May Concern, Please find attached my application for the scholarship.
examples.cn: 致相关负责人：请查收我附上的奖学金申请。

grammar.explain: 在正式信件的结尾，通常会使用“Sincerely”或“Regards”作为结束语，后面跟着你的全名。这同样是表达礼貌和专业。

reading.cn:
梅正在帮她的朋友薇起草一封致学校的重要邮件。薇有一些关于即将到来的入学程序的问题，需要一个官方的答复。梅，由于学到了很多关于正式写作的知识，她开始写邮件：“To Whom It May Concern,”

“开得好头，梅，”薇说，“听起来很专业。”

梅继续写道：“我的名字是梅玲，代表未来的学生陈薇写此邮件。我们写信是为了询问下一个学年的入学要求。具体来说，我们想澄清所需文件和申请截止日期。您的及时回复将不胜感激。”

薇审阅了一下。“完美！这封邮件既礼貌又清晰，而且直奔主题。谢谢你的帮助，梅！”
reading.en:
Mei was helping her friend Wei draft an important email to the school. Wei had some questions about the upcoming admissions procedure and needed an official answer. Mei, having learned a lot about formal writing, began the email: "To Whom It May Concern," 

"That's a good start, Mei," Wei said. "It sounds very professional." 

Mei continued, "My name is Mei Ling, writing on behalf of Wei Chen, a prospective student. We are writing to inquire about the admission requirements for the next academic year. Specifically, we would like to clarify the documents needed and the application deadlines. Your prompt response would be greatly appreciated." 

Wei reviewed it. "Perfect! It's polite, clear, and gets straight to the point. Thank you for your help, Mei!"

Mei added a closing, "Sincerely, Mei Ling." She then explained to Wei the importance of using formal language and proper salutations and closings when writing to institutions like schools. "It shows respect and ensures your message is taken seriously," Mei advised.
reading.cn: 梅又加上了结尾：“Sincerely, Mei Ling.” 然后她向薇解释了在给学校等机构写信时使用正式语言和恰当的称谓与结尾的重要性。“这表达了尊重，并确保你的信息被认真对待，”梅建议道。
薇对发送这封邮件感到更有信心了。“我从你身上学到了很多，”薇说。“这些正式表达真的很有用。”
reading.en: Wei felt much more confident about sending the email. "I learned a lot from watching you," Wei said. "These formal expressions are really useful."
Mei smiled. "It's all about practice. And knowing when to use 'To Whom It May Concern' is key!"
reading.cn: 梅笑了。“这都与练习有关。而且知道何时使用‘To Whom It May Concern’是关键！”
梅昨天刚到美国。这是她在寄宿家庭的第一个早晨。她醒得很早。“现在几点？”她心想。梅看了看钟。钟上显示凌晨 3:00。“哦，不！太早了，”梅说。她有倒时差。她试图回去睡觉，但睡不着。她现在饿了。她悄悄地走到厨房。她的寄宿妈妈史密斯夫人已经在那里了。
reading.en: Mei just arrived in the U.S. yesterday. It's her first morning in her host family's home. She wakes up very early. "What time is it?" she thinks. Mei looks at the clock. It says 3:00 AM. "Oh, no! It's too early," Mei says. She has jet lag. She tries to go back to sleep, but she can't. She is hungry now. She quietly goes to the kitchen. Mrs. Smith, her host mom, is already there.
Mrs. Smith: Good morning, Mei! You're up early.

grammar.explain: 动名词（-ing 形式）可以作句子的主语或宾语，表示一个动作或行为。当用作主语时，它通常表示一种状态或行为本身。当用作宾语时，它可以跟在某些动词或介词后面。

listening.audio: Ivan Dmitrich, a middle-class man who lived with his family on a small income, went to bed early one evening. After dinner, he read the newspaper. He remembered that his wife had a lottery ticket, bought many weeks ago. She had forgotten all about it. He wondered, "What if we actually win?" The series was 9,499, and the number was 26. He quickly looked at the newspaper to check the winning list. "Good heavens! 9,499 is there! And 26 is also there!" He couldn't believe his eyes. His wife, Masha, was sitting at the table, folding laundry. He handed her the newspaper. Masha's face turned pale. "It is our ticket!" she cried. They both started to imagine their new life. They would buy an estate with the money, maybe a house and some land. They would travel, eat delicious food, and live a life of luxury. Their excitement grew. But then, a different thought came to Ivan. "What if Masha tries to take all the money for herself?" he wondered. He started to feel annoyed with her. Masha, in turn, began to think about how Ivan might spend the money on his hobbies, ignoring her needs. They started to argue about how the money would be spent, even before they officially had it. "It's my ticket!" Masha shouted. "I bought it!" Ivan replied, "But I work hard to earn the money that bought it!" Their dreams of a happy, rich life together quickly turned into anger and resentment. The dream of the lottery win had ruined their peaceful evening.

reading.en: Ivan Dmitrich, a middle-class man who lived with his family on a small income, went to bed early one evening. After dinner, he read the newspaper. He remembered that his wife had a lottery ticket, bought many weeks ago. She had forgotten all about it.

reading.cn: “万一我们真的中奖了呢？”他想。“系列是9499，号码是26。”他迅速查看报纸上的中奖名单。“天哪！9499在那里！26也在那里！”他简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。他的妻子玛莎正坐在桌子旁叠衣服。他把报纸递给了她。
reading.en: “What if we actually win?” he wondered. “The series is 9,499, and the number is 26.” He quickly looked at the newspaper to check the winning list. “Good heavens! 9,499 is there! And 26 is also there!” He couldn't believe his eyes. His wife, Masha, was sitting at the table, folding laundry. He handed her the newspaper.

reading.cn: 玛莎的脸色变得苍白。“是我们的彩票！”她喊道。他们两人开始想象他们的新生活。他们会用这笔钱买一个房地产，也许是一所房子和一些土地。他们会去旅行，吃美味的食物，过上奢侈的生活。他们的兴奋之情越来越高涨。

But then, a different thought came to Ivan. “What if Masha tries to take all the money for herself?” he wondered. He started to feel annoyed with her. Masha, in turn, began to think about how Ivan might spend the money on his hobbies, ignoring her needs. They started to argue about how the money would be spent, even before they officially had it.
reading.cn: 但是，伊万突然有了另一个想法。“如果玛莎想把所有的钱都据为己有呢？”他想。他开始对她感到恼火。玛莎反过来也开始想伊万可能会把钱花在自己的爱好上，而忽视她的需求。他们开始争论这笔钱会如何花费，甚至在他们正式得到它之前。

grammar.title: 定语从句 (Relative Clauses) - 用 which 引导非限制性定语从句
grammar.explain: 定语从句用来修饰名词或代词，提供更多信息。非限制性定语从句提供补充信息，即使没有它，句子的主句意思也是完整的。它通常用逗号与主句隔开，修饰物时常用 "which" 引导。

grammar.title: 投诉表达 - 礼貌地反映问题
grammar.explain: 虽然本课场景是愉快的感恩节,但为了单元主题的完整性,我们也学习一些关于“投诉”的礼貌表达。在日常生活中,如果遇到需要反映问题的情况,我们可以用这些句型。

output.sample: Hey Lily! Guess what? I just had my first Thanksgiving dinner, and it was amazing! The Walkers are so nice. We had a huge turkey and tons of other delicious food. My favorite was definitely the stuffing, which was Mrs. Walker's secret recipe. It was so flavorful! And the whole dinner, which lasted for almost four hours, was full of laughter. I'm so full and happy now! Hope you had a great day too!
output.prompt: 你刚刚在Walker家度过了你的第一个感恩节。给你的好朋友写一条短信,分享你的感受和你最喜欢的一道菜。至少使用一个以 "which" 引导的非限制性定语从句。
output.cn: 你第一次在美国的寄宿家庭Walker家过感恩节。给你的好朋友发短信,分享你的感受和你最喜欢的一道菜。至少使用一个以“which”引导的非限制性定语从句。

reading.cn: 梅、她的妈妈和爸爸在沃克家享用感恩节晚餐。这是梅在美国过的第一个感恩节。沃克太太做了一只巨大的火鸡,闻起来很棒。沃克先生切火鸡,这是他每年都乐在其中的传统。
reading.en: Mei, her mother, and her father were at the Walkers' for Thanksgiving dinner. It was Mei's first Thanksgiving in America. Mrs. Walker had cooked a huge turkey, which smelled wonderful. Mr. Walker carved the turkey, which was a tradition he enjoyed every year.

reading.cn: 梅感到非常感激。这顿持续了将近四个小时的晚餐,充满了美味的食物和愉快的交谈。他们吃了火鸡、土豆泥、四季豆砂锅和蔓越莓酱。填料是沃克太太的独家秘方,是梅的最爱。
reading.en: Mei felt very grateful. The dinner, which lasted almost four hours, was full of delicious food and lively conversation. They had turkey, mashed potatoes, green bean casserole, and cranberry sauce. The stuffing, which was Mrs. Walker's special recipe, was Mei's favorite.

reading.cn: 晚餐后,沃克太太端出了南瓜派和苹果派作为甜点。“这绝对是一顿我永远不会忘记的感恩节晚餐,”梅后来告诉妈妈。“一切都太棒了,沃克一家人太好了!”
reading.en: After dinner, Mrs. Walker brought out pumpkin pie and apple pie for dessert. "This is definitely a Thanksgiving dinner which I will never forget," Mei told her mother later. "Everything was so good, and the Walkers are so kind!"

reading.cn: 梅的妈妈笑了。“是的，确实如此。我们很幸运有这么好的主人。”
reading.en: Mei's mom smiled. "Yes, it truly was. We are so lucky to have such wonderful hosts."

grammar.title: 使役动词：let / make / help + 宾语 + 动词原形

grammar.title: 动词原形的用法回顾

reading.cn: 大家好！今天我们来聊点有趣的事。你的父母有没有让你做过你真心想做的事？或者让你做过你不想做的事？有时候，他们只是帮助了你，对吗？
reading.en: Hello everyone! Today, let's talk about something interesting. Have your parents ever let you do something you really wanted to do? Or maybe made you do something you didn't want to do? And sometimes, they just helped you, right?

reading.cn: 例如，我16岁的时候，我妈妈第一次让我开她的车。我太兴奋了！但有时，我爸爸会让我打扫房间，即使我想玩电子游戏。那不是很有趣。我的奶奶总是帮我做作业，尤其是数学。我很幸运能得到她的帮助。
reading.en: For example, when I was 16, my mom let me drive her car for the first time. I was so excited! But sometimes, my dad would make me clean my room, even when I wanted to play video games. That wasn't fun. And my grandma always helped me with my homework, especially math. I was so lucky to have her help.

reading.cn: 这些词——let、make 和 help——非常有用。我们用它们来谈论别人允许我们做什么，强迫我们做什么，或者帮助我们做什么。注意它们是如何与另一个动词一起使用的。这是英语中表达动作的常见方式。
reading.en: These words – let, make, and help – are very useful. We use them to talk about what people allow us to do, force us to do, or assist us with. Pay attention to how they are used with another verb. It's a common way to express actions in English.

reading.cn: 那么你呢？你的父母让你做了什么？他们让你做了什么？他们又帮助你做了什么？
reading.en: So, what about you? What did your parents let you do? What did they make you do? And what did they help you with?

output.sample: Have you heard the news? My cousin, who applied for a scholarship to study abroad, just got it! That’s awesome! The scholarship, which will cover all her tuition fees, is a huge help. I’m so happy for her; she’s been working so hard for this.

reading.cn: 梅在寄宿家庭住了几个月了。她一直有个秘密没有告诉他们，一个关于她未来的重要决定。
reading.en: Mei has been living with her host family for a few months now. She has a secret that she's been keeping from them, a big decision about her future.

reading.cn: 一天晚上，在晚餐时，梅终于鼓起勇气。她的心怦怦直跳。她开口说：“有件事我需要告诉大家。”史密斯夫人和蔼地笑着说：“是什么事，亲爱的？”梅深吸一口气。“我决定申请在美国攻读硕士学位。我后悔没有早点告诉你们。”
reading.en: One evening, at dinner, Mei finally gathers her courage. Her heart is pounding. She starts, "There's something I need to tell you all." Mrs. Smith smiles kindly, "What is it, dear?" Mei takes a deep breath. "I've decided to apply for a master's degree here in the US. I regret not telling you sooner."

reading.cn: 史密斯先生看起来很惊讶，然后脸上露出温暖的笑容。“梅，这真是个好消息！我们为你感到骄傲。你为什么要后悔呢？我们在这里支持你。”
reading.en: Mr. Smith looks surprised, then a warm smile spreads across his face. "Mei, that's wonderful news! We're so proud of you. Why would you regret it? We're here to support you."

reading.cn: 梅的眼睛里涌出了泪水。“我很紧张。我以为你们可能不会理解，或者会觉得麻烦。”史密斯夫人隔着桌子握住梅的手。“绝不会的，梅。你的梦想对我们很重要。我们会尽一切可能帮助你。”
reading.en: Mei's eyes well up with tears. "I was nervous. I thought maybe you wouldn't understand, or that it would be a bother." Mrs. Smith reaches across the table to hold Mei's hand. "Never, Mei. Your dreams are important to us. We'll help you in any way we can."

reading.cn: 梅感到肩上的巨大重担卸了下来。她很感激他们的理解和支持。她意识到，有时候，最难的部分仅仅是开口说出来。
reading.en: Mei feels a huge weight lift from her shoulders. She's grateful for their understanding and support. She realizes that sometimes, the hardest part is just saying it.

grammar.explain:
当我们需要转述别人说的话，特别是命令或请求时，我们通常使用“间接命令”结构。核心句型是：
Subject + tell/ask + Object + (not) to + Verb (原形)

examples.cn: 她对我说：“别担心。” → 她让我别担心。
examples.en: She told me, “Don't worry.” → She told me not to worry.

examples.cn: 他对我说：“请在这里等。” → 他让我等在那里。
examples.en: He said to me, “Please wait here.” → He asked me to wait there.

examples.cn: 老师告诉我们：“完成作业。” → 老师让我们完成作业。
examples.en: The teacher told us, “Finish your homework.” → The teacher told us to finish our homework.

reading.cn: 梅觉得胃里一阵紧张。她需要一封强有力的推荐信来申请她梦想中的硕士项目，而且截止日期很快就要到了。她唯一能求助的人是萨拉，她的前经理，萨拉总是对梅的工作评价很高。
reading.en: Mei felt a knot of anxiety tighten in her stomach. She needed a strong recommendation letter for her dream master's program, and the deadline was approaching fast. There was only one person she could ask: Sarah, her former manager, who always spoke highly of Mei's work.

reading.cn: 鼓起勇气，梅给萨拉打了电话。解释了情况后，她紧张地问道：“萨拉，你能帮我写一封强有力的推荐信吗？我将不胜感激。”萨拉耐心地听着。然后，她用温暖而令人安心的语气告诉梅，让她别担心。
reading.en: Gathering her courage, Mei called Sarah. After explaining her situation, she nervously asked, “Would you be able to write me a strong recommendation letter, Sarah? I’d really appreciate it.” Sarah listened patiently. Then, with a warm and reassuring tone, she told Mei not to worry.

reading.cn: “当然，梅！我很乐意。”萨拉说，“你是一个优秀的员工，我一直都知道你前途光明。把你认为我应该知道的所有细节都发给我，我会确保突出你的优点。”梅立刻感到一阵轻松。萨拉让她在本周末前发送细节，并承诺在截止日期前提交推荐信。梅非常感谢萨拉，对她的申请也更有信心了。
reading.en: “Of course, Mei! I’d be happy to,” Sarah said. “You were an excellent employee, and I always knew you had a bright future. Just send me all the details you think I should know, and I’ll make sure to highlight your strengths.” Mei felt an immediate sense of relief. Sarah told her to send the details by the end of the week, and promised to submit the letter before the deadline. Mei thanked Sarah profusely, feeling much more confident about her application.

reading.cn: 那天晚些时候，梅回忆起萨拉的话。*她让我别担心。*这些话在她脑海中回荡，缓解了她的紧张。她知道自己很幸运。
reading.en: Later that day, Mei recalled Sarah's words. *She told me not to worry.* Those words echoed in her mind, easing her nerves. She knew she was in good hands.

reading.en: One dollar and eighty-seven cents. That was all. And sixty cents of it was in pennies. Pennies saved one and two at a time by bargaining with the grocer and the vegetable man and the butcher until one's cheeks burned with the silent imputation of parsimony that such close dealing implied. Three times Della counted it. One dollar and eighty-seven cents. And the next day would be Christmas.
reading.cn: 一美元八十七美分。仅此而已。其中六十美分是零钱。一分两分地从杂货店老板、蔬菜商和肉店老板那里讨价还价省下来的，每当这样斤斤计较时，她的脸颊都会因那种不言而喻的吝啬指责而发烫。黛拉数了三次。一美元八十七美分。而第二天就是圣诞节了。

reading.en: There was nothing to do but flop down on the shabby little couch and wail. So Della did it. Which instigates the moral reflection that life is made up of sobs, sniffles, and smiles, with sniffles predominating. While Jim was out, Della decided to sell her beautiful long hair, which was her most cherished possession, to buy him a Christmas gift.
reading.cn: 除了倒在破旧的小沙发上哭泣，别无他法。黛拉照做了。这引发了一个道德反思，即生命是由哭泣、抽噎和微笑组成的，其中抽噎占据主导地位。吉姆出门期间，黛拉决定卖掉她美丽的秀发，那是她最珍视的财产，为他买一份圣诞礼物。
吉姆回家时，看到黛拉头发变短了。他只是盯着她，没有生气，但表情很奇怪。黛拉解释说她卖了头发是为了给他买礼物。然后吉姆笑了，给了她一个包裹。里面是一套漂亮的梳子，黛拉一直很喜欢。
reading.en: When Jim came home, he saw Della with her short hair. He just stared at her, not with anger, but with a strange expression. Della explained that she sold her hair to buy him a gift. Then Jim smiled and gave her a parcel. Inside was a set of beautiful combs, which Della had admired for a long time.

Della then presented Jim with his gift: a beautiful platinum chain for his treasured gold watch. But Jim had also sold his watch to buy Della's combs. They looked at each other, realizing the great sacrifices they had made. But they knew their gifts, though momentarily useless, were tokens of their immense love.
reading.cn: 黛拉随后将礼物送给吉姆：一条精美的白金表链给他珍贵的金表。但吉姆也卖掉了他的手表去买黛拉的梳子。他们互相看着，意识到他们所做的巨大牺牲。但他们知道，他们的礼物，尽管暂时无用，却是他们巨大爱情的象征。
麦琪（东方三博士），你知道的，是智者——非常智慧的人——他们给马槽里的圣婴带来了礼物。他们开创了赠送圣诞礼物的艺术。他们是智者，他们的礼物无疑是明智的，也许还带有在重复时可以交换的特权。而在这里，我笨拙地讲述了公寓里两个“愚蠢”的孩子平凡的经历，他们最不明智地为彼此牺牲了家中最大的珍宝。但在最后，我要对如今的智者说，在所有赠送和接受礼物的人中，这两个人是最聪明的。
reading.en: The Magi, as you know, were wise men—wonderfully wise men—who brought gifts to the Babe in the manger. They invented the art of giving Christmas presents. Being wise, their gifts were no doubt wise ones, possibly bearing the privilege of exchange in case of duplication. And here I have lamely related to you the uneventful chronicle of two foolish children in an apartment who most unwisely sacrificed for each other the greatest treasures of their house. But in a last word to the wise of these days let it be said that of all who give and receive gifts, these two were the wisest.

output.sample: The most impressive aspect of the story for me is the selfless love between Della and Jim. They both gave up their most prized possessions just to buy a gift for the other, which shows how much they cherished each other. It’s a powerful message that true love is about sacrifice, not about the material value of gifts. Their actions, though seemingly foolish, were the wisest because they were driven by pure love.

reading.en: Mei is studying for the GRE, a very important and challenging exam for her graduate school application. She’s at her desk, surrounded by textbooks and notes, trying to focus on complex math problems. Suddenly, her phone rings.
reading.cn: 梅正在为GRE考试而学习，这是她申请研究生院一个非常重要且有挑战性的考试。她坐在书桌前，周围是课本和笔记，试图专注于复杂的数学题。突然，她的电话响了。

reading.en: She sighs, seeing her father’s name on the caller ID. This is the third time he’s called today. Mei loves her dad, but his frequent calls are becoming a major distraction. She really needs to concentrate.
reading.cn: 她叹了口气，看到来电显示是她爸爸的名字。这已经是她爸爸今天打来的第三个电话了。梅爱她的爸爸，但他频繁的电话成了主要的干扰。她真的需要集中注意力。

reading.en: She answers, trying to sound cheerful. “Hi, Dad! Everything okay?”
reading.cn: 她接了电话，努力听起来很开心。“嗨，爸爸！一切都好吗？”
她爸爸开始长篇大论地讲他的一天。梅努力耐心地听着，但她的目光却不停地回到她的课本上。她感到一股挫败感油然而生。
reading.en: Her father launches into a long story about his day. Mei tries to listen patiently, but her eyes keep drifting back to her textbooks. She feels a rising sense of frustration.

reading.cn: 电话结束后，梅把手机调成了静音。“我希望他别打这么多电话，”她自言自语道，“我希望我能专心学习。”她知道爸爸是好意，但她希望他能理解这个考试有多么严格。
reading.en: After the call, Mei puts her phone on silent. “I wish he would stop calling so much,” she mutters to herself. “I wish I could just focus on my studies.” She knows he means well, but she wishes he understood how demanding this exam is.

listening.audio: Mei is studying for the GRE, a very important and challenging exam for her graduate school application. She’s at her desk, surrounded by textbooks and notes, trying to focus on complex math problems. Suddenly, her phone rings. She sighs, seeing her father’s name on the caller ID. This is the third time he’s called today. Mei loves her dad, but his frequent calls are becoming a major distraction. She really needs to concentrate. She answers, trying to sound cheerful. “Hi, Dad! Everything okay?” Her father launches into a long story about his day. Mei tries to listen patiently, but her eyes keep drifting back to her textbooks. She feels a rising sense of frustration. After the call, Mei puts her phone on silent. “I wish he would stop calling so much,” she mutters to herself. “I wish I could just focus on my studies.” She knows he means well, but she wishes he understood how demanding this exam is.

B: Sure, what's up?
A: Well, I've noticed you often stay up very late watching videos, and the light from your screen sometimes makes it hard for me to fall asleep. I'm really trying to get enough rest for my classes.

A: Using your phone with the brightness down would be great, if you don't mind. I'd really appreciate it.

reading.en: Mei was trying to study for her English test in her room. Her roommate, Vivi, was listening to music without headphones, and singing along loudly. Mei tried to ignore it at first, but the music was too loud. She took a deep breath and decided to talk to Vivi.
reading.cn: 梅正在房间里努力学习英语，准备考试。她的室友薇薇没有戴耳机，大声地听歌并跟着唱。梅一开始想忍住，但音乐实在太响了。她深吸一口气，决定和薇薇谈谈。

reading.en: "Vivi," Mei said politely, "I'm really trying to focus on my studies, but the music is making it hard for me to concentrate." Vivi took off her headphones, looking surprised. "Oh, I'm so sorry, Mei! I didn't realize it was bothering you. I can turn it down, or use my headphones." Mei smiled. "Headphones would be great, if you don't mind. I really appreciate it." Vivi nodded. "No problem at all! I totally understand. I'll be more careful next time." Mei felt relieved. It was a small step, but an important one in learning to live with a roommate.
reading.cn: “薇薇，”梅礼貌地说，“我真的在努力学习，但是音乐太吵了，我很难集中注意力。”薇薇摘下耳机，看起来很惊讶。“哦，真对不起，梅！我没意识到这打扰到你了。我可以把声音调小点，或者用耳机。”梅笑了。“如果你不介意的话，戴耳机就太好了。我真的很感谢。”薇薇点点头。“一点问题都没有！我完全理解。下次我会更注意的。”梅松了口气。这是很小的一步，但对学习如何与室友相处来说，却是重要的一步。

grammar.explain: “Need to + 动词原形”表示需要做某事，强调一种必要性或义务。这在日常生活中非常常用，用来表达你必须完成的任务或解决的问题。

grammar.title: Get + 宾语 + 过去分词 (I need to get my car fixed.)
grammar.explain: 这是一个常见的被动语态结构，表示“找人做某事”或“让某事被完成”。在这里，主语“I”并没有亲自修理车，而是找了别人来修理。

quiz.q: What happened to Mei's car?

output.sample: My laptop suddenly stopped working last week. I need to get it fixed because I use it for work every day. I called a repair shop and asked for an estimate. They said it would take a few days to deal with the problem. Oh no, not now, I thought! I really need this laptop.
output.cn: 说一说你需要修理/处理某件事的经历。比如：手机坏了、电脑出故障了、需要处理一份紧急文件等等。你是怎么处理的？运用本课学到的词汇和句型。

reading.cn: 梅开车去上班，感觉有点心不在焉。突然，她的旧车开始发出奇怪的声音，然后在一 L条安静的街道中间彻底抛锚了。“哦不，偏偏是现在！”她叹了口气。她给她的朋友丽莎打了电话。
reading.en: Mei was driving to work, feeling a little distracted. Suddenly, her old car started making a strange noise and then completely broke down in the middle of a quiet street. "Oh no, not now!" she sighed. She called her friend, Lisa.

reading.cn: 梅：“嗨，丽莎，我的车抛锚了。我得把它修一下。你认识好的机械师吗？”
reading.en: Mei: "Hi Lisa, my car just broke down. I need to get it fixed. Do you know a good mechanic?"
Lisa: "Oh no, Mei! That’s terrible. My mechanic, Joe, is pretty reliable. He works at 'Speedy Auto Repair'. I can give you his number. You'll need to call a tow truck first to get your car there."
reading.cn: 丽莎：“哦不，梅！这太糟糕了。我的机械师乔，人挺靠谱的。他在'飞速汽车修理'工作。我能把他的电话给你。你得先叫辆拖车把你的车弄过去。”

reading.en: Mei: "Thanks, Lisa! I'll do that. I hope it's not too expensive. I really need this car for work. This is just one more thing I have to deal with today."
reading.cn: 梅：“谢谢，丽莎！我会的。我希望不要太贵。我工作真的需要这辆车。这只是我今天必须处理的又一件事。”

reading.en: Lisa: "I understand. He usually gives a fair estimate. Just make sure to tell him I sent you. And maybe take a deep breath. Things will get better."
reading.cn: 丽莎：“我明白。他通常会给一个合理的估价。你一定要告诉他是我介绍你去的。也许深呼吸一下。事情会好起来的。”

grammar.explain: “If only” 和 “I wish” 都用来表达对现在或过去情况的强烈愿望、遗憾或后悔。它们后面跟着虚拟语气。
grammar.title: 虚拟语气：表示强烈愿望或遗憾 (If only / I wish...)
“If only” 的用法

examples.cn: 要是我更高些就好了。 (对现在事实的假设)
examples.en: If only I were taller.

examples.cn: 要是我当时听了你的建议就好了。 (对过去事实的后悔)
examples.en: If only I had listened to your advice.

grammar.explain: “If only” 的语气比 “I wish” 更强烈，常用来表达对事与愿违的强烈遗憾。

examples.cn: 我希望我能飞。 (对现在无法实现愿望)
examples.en: I wish I could fly.

examples.cn: 我希望你不要离开。 (对现在事实的遗憾)
examples.en: I wish you weren’t leaving.

grammar.explain: “I wish” 同样表达愿望或遗憾，但语气可能稍弱。

listening.audio: It’s the night before Mei’s application deadline. She’s been working on her essay for hours, but she still feels like it’s not perfect. She sighs, looking at the clock. It’s already 11 PM. “If only I had more time,” she mumbles to herself. “Then I could review everything one more time, maybe even rewrite a paragraph. I wish I had started earlier. Now I’m so stressed.” She thinks about all the other things she could have done. “If only I hadn’t spent so much time on social media this week. If only I had focused more in class instead of daydreaming. I regret wasting so much time.” Mei takes a deep breath. She knows there’s no turning back now. “It is what it is. I just need to submit it. I wish I felt more confident, but I’ve done my best.”

reading.cn: 她想着所有她本可以做的其他事情。“要是这周我没在社交媒体上花那么多时间就好了。要是上课时我更专注一些，而不是白日做梦就好了。我后悔浪费了那么多时间。”

Dear Diary,

It’s almost midnight, and my application essay is still not perfect. I feel so overwhelmed. If only I had more time, I could make it better! reading.en: One hot summer day, a hungry and thirsty wolf decided to quench his thirst at a clear stream. As he was about to drink, he noticed a little lamb further downstream, also enjoying the cool water.
reading.cn: 一个炎热的夏日，一只又饿又渴的狼决定到一条清澈的小溪边解渴。正当它准备喝水时，它注意到下游有一只小羊，也正在享受着凉爽的水。
“你竟敢！”狼低声咆哮道，眼睛里燃烧着怒火。“你把我的饮用水弄浑了！我不会让你把我的水弄脏的！”
reading.en: "How dare you!" growled the wolf, his eyes blazing with anger. "You are muddying my drinking water! I won't have you spoiling my drink!"
The innocent lamb, trembling with fear, replied, "But, kind sir, that's impossible. The water flows from you to me. I couldn't possibly muddy your water, as it starts from your end."
reading.cn: 无辜的小羊吓得发抖，回答说：“但是，好先生，那不可能啊。水是从您那里流向我这里的。我不可能弄浑您的水，因为水是从您那边开始流的。”
然而，狼不是一个能讲道理的。“没关系！”它咆哮道，“六个月前，你侮辱了我爸爸！”
reading.en: The wolf, however, was not one to be reasoned with. "No matter!" he snarled. "Six months ago, you insulted my father!"
The lamb, confused, protested, "But six months ago, I wasn't even born!"
reading.cn: 小羊困惑地抗议道：“可是六个月前，我都还没出生呢！”

listening.audio: One hot summer day, a hungry and thirsty wolf decided to quench his thirst at a clear stream. As he was about to drink, he noticed a little lamb further downstream, also enjoying the cool water. "How dare you!" growled the wolf, his eyes blazing with anger. "You are muddying my drinking water! I won't have you spoiling my drink!" The innocent lamb, trembling with fear, replied, "But, kind sir, that's impossible. The water flows from you to me. I couldn't possibly muddy your water, as it starts from your end." The wolf, however, was not one to be reasoned with. "No matter!" he snarled. "Six months ago, you insulted my father!" The lamb, confused, protested, "But six months ago, I wasn't even born!" The wolf, finding no true fault with the lamb, still would not let it go. "Well, if it wasn't you, it was your brother!" he cried. "I have no brother," said the lamb. "Then," said the wolf, "it was your ancestor! Be that as it may, I'm not going without my dinner!" And without another word, he fell upon the poor, helpless lamb and devoured it.

The wolf **made the lamb tremble** with fear.
examples.cn: 狼让小羊吓得发抖。 (make + 宾语 + 动词原形，表示强迫或导致某事发生)
我父母让我自己选择衣服。(let + 宾语 + 动词原形，表示允许某事发生)
examples.en: My parents **let me choose** my own clothes.

grammar.title: 使役动词 (Causative Verbs): let, have, make
grammar.explain: 使役动词用于表达“让/使某人做某事”的句型。在《狼与小羊》的故事中，狼试图“让小羊承担责任”，或者“使小羊的水变浑”。

grammar.title: 分词短语 (Participial Phrases) 作状语
grammar.explain: 分词短语（现在分词或过去分词构成）可以作状语，修饰主句的谓语或整个句子，说明原因、时间、方式或伴随情况。它们使得句子更简洁生动。

examples.cn: 因为害怕而发抖，无辜的小羊回答说…… (现在分词短语作状语，表示伴随状态或原因)
examples.en: **Trembling with fear**, the innocent lamb replied...

examples.cn: 因为又饿又渴，狼寻找一条小溪。(现在分词短语作原因状语)
examples.en: **Being hungry and thirsty**, the wolf looked for a stream.

examples.cn: 看到小羊后，狼的眼睛燃烧着怒火。(现在分词短语作时间状语)
examples.en: **Seeing the lamb**, the wolf's eyes blazed with anger.

examples.cn: 小羊，正在享受着凉水，一开始没注意到狼。(现在分词短语作定语，修饰 lamb)
examples.en: The lamb, **enjoying the cool water**, didn't notice the wolf at first.
The **growling** wolf tried to blame the lamb.
examples.cn: 咆哮的狼试图责怪小羊。(现在分词作定语修饰 wolf)
受惊的小羊迅速离开了。(过去分词作定语修饰 lamb)
examples.en: The **frightened** lamb quickly moved away.

grammar.title: 分词短语 (Participial Phrases) 作定语
grammar.explain: 分词短语也可以作定语，修饰名词或代词，相当于一个定语从句。在《狼与小羊》的故事中，我们可以用分词短语来描述事物的特征。

output.sample: The wolf was extremely cruel and unjust. Being consumed by hunger, he made up various excuses to blame the innocent lamb. He wouldn't let the lamb explain itself, showing no mercy. His actions, driven by pure selfishness, allowed him to devour the lamb without a second thought.
output.prompt: 你认为狼的行为可以用哪个词来形容？请用英文写一段话，至少包含一个使役动词和一个分词短语。
output.cn: 你认为狼的行为可以用哪个词来形容？请用英文写一段话，至少包含一个使役动词和一个分词短语。

examples.cn: 做完作业后，我出去玩了。
examples.en: Having finished my homework, I went out to play.

examples.cn: 努力学习后，她轻松通过了考试。
examples.en: Having studied hard, she passed the exam easily.

examples.cn: 因为累了，他早早地睡了。
examples.en: Being tired, he went to bed early.

examples.cn: 她灿烂地笑着接过了奖项。
examples.en: Smiling brightly, she accepted the award.

grammar.title: Using Participle Phrases for Cause and Effect / Time
grammar.explain:
本课的核心句型 “Having waited for weeks, I finally got the email.” 中， “Having waited for weeks” 是一个分词短语，用作状语，说明主句动作发生的原因或者时间顺序。它可以用来简化句子，使表达更紧凑，常用于表示：
1. 完成某事后发生另一个动作。
2. 某事导致了另一个结果。

grammar.title: Mixed Conditionals (Third Conditional + Present Result)
grammar.explain: 在一些情况下，我们谈论过去未发生的事情对现在造成的影响。这叫做混合条件句，结合了第三条件句（If + had + P.P.）和第二条件句（would + V）。

examples.cn: 如果我大学时学习更努力，我现在就会有一份更好的工作了。（过去未发生，现在有影响）
examples.en: If I had studied harder in college, I would have a better job now.

examples.cn: 如果梅没有申请那所大学，她今天就不会庆祝她的录取了。（过去未发生，现在有影响）
examples.en: If Mei hadn't applied to that university, she wouldn't be celebrating her admission today.

examples.cn: 如果他没错过航班，他现在就在巴黎了。
examples.en: If he hadn't missed the flight, he would be in Paris right now.

examples.cn: 我还在等公司回复我的工作申请。
examples.en: I'm still waiting to hear back from the company about my job application.

examples.cn: 你收到房东关于公寓的回复了吗？
examples.en: Did you hear back from the landlord about the apartment?

examples.cn: 梅终于收到大学的回复，非常兴奋。
examples.en: Mei was so excited to finally hear back from the university.

grammar.title: Phrasal Verb: 'Hear back from'
grammar.explain: “Hear back from” 是一个常用短语动词，意思是“收到（某人或机构的）回复”。这在申请大学、工作或其他需要等待官方回复的场景中非常常见。

output.sample: Having waited for months, I finally received the acceptance letter from my dream university. My heart was pounding, and I felt incredibly relieved. When I saw 'Congratulations!', a huge smile spread across my face. I immediately called my parents to share the good news. All my hard work has paid off!
output.prompt: 你大学申请结果出来了吗？你收到的是什么邮件？是录取通知吗？收到时是什么心情？用英文写一小段话描述一下。
output.cn: 想象一下你收到大学录取通知书的那一刻，或者其他你期待已久的好消息。描述一下你当时的心情、你看到了什么、做了什么。

reading.cn: 梅已经等了好几周，期盼能收到大学的回复。她每天都查看邮件，希望能看到好消息。她的朋友们不断告诉她要耐心，但这很难。她感到既兴奋又紧张。
reading.en: Mei had been waiting for weeks to hear back from the university. Every day, she checked her email, hoping to see good news. Her friends kept telling her to be patient, but it was hard. She felt a mix of excitement and nervousness.

reading.cn: 然后，一个早上，它发生了。等了好几周，梅终于收到了邮件。她打开邮件时心怦怦直跳。她看到的第一个词是“恭喜！”这是她首选大学的录取通知，还附带了部分奖学金！
reading.en: Then, one morning, it happened. Having waited for weeks, Mei finally got the email. Her heart pounded as she opened it. The first word she saw was 'Congratulations!' It was an admission offer from her top-choice university, with a partial scholarship!

reading.cn: 她脸上绽开一个大大的笑容。“太棒了！”她小声说道。她立刻打电话给父母，他们也同样激动。后来，她把邮件转发给了她最好的朋友，朋友回复了一串快乐的表情符号。梅感到无比宽慰和自豪。她所有的努力都得到了回报。
reading.en: A huge smile spread across her face. 'Yes!' she whispered. She immediately called her parents, who were just as thrilled. Later, she forwarded the email to her best friend, who replied with a string of happy emojis. Mei felt incredibly relieved and proud. All her hard work had paid off.

listening.audio: Dear Anna, as I prepare to leave, I find myself thinking about how much you've helped me during my stay here. It feels like just yesterday I arrived, a bit lost and unsure. But it was you who welcomed me with open arms and made me feel at home. There were times when I faced challenges, and it was your encouragement that kept me going. grammar.title: 强调句型: It is/was...who/that...

examples.cn: 是安娜救了我。（强调了“Anna”这个主语）

grammar.explain: 当我们想要强调句子的某个部分（比如主语、宾语或时间状语）时，可以使用“It is/was...who/that...”句型。被强调的部分放在is/was和who/that之间。

reading.en: Mei's mother, Wei, was having a serious talk with her daughter. "Mei, your host family is ready for you to move in. Are you sure you're ready to be more independent?" Wei asked, trying to sound supportive, but her worry was clear.
reading.cn: 梅的妈妈薇正在和女儿认真谈话。“梅，你的寄宿家庭已经准备好让你搬进去了。你确定你准备好变得更独立了吗？”薇问道，努力地让自己听起来支持女儿，但她的担忧显而易见。

reading.en: Mei nodded. "Mom, I know you're worried, but I want to try. Living with a host family will be a great experience for me. I can learn to take care of myself and practice my English more." she explained.
reading.cn: 梅点了点头。“妈，我知道你担心，但我想试试。住在寄宿家庭对我来说将是很棒的经历。我能学会照顾自己，并且更多地练习英语。”她解释道。
薇叹了口气。“我理解你对独立的渴望，梅。但我会想你的。对我来说，放手很难。”她承认道，声音变得柔和。
reading.en: Wei sighed. "I understand your desire for independence, Mei. But I'll miss you. It's hard for me to let go." she admitted, her voice softening.
Mei walked over and hugged her mom. "I'll visit every weekend, Mom. And we can call each other every day. Let's meet halfway. You let me try this, and I promise to keep in touch." Mei suggested.
reading.cn: 梅走过去抱住妈妈。“我每个周末都会回来看您，妈妈。我们也可以每天打电话。咱们各让一步吧。您让我试试，我保证会保持联系的。”梅提议道。
薇笑了，一滴眼泪滚下脸颊。“好吧，梅。咱们各让一步吧。我放你走，但你必须答应要安全快乐。”她同意了。
reading.en: Wei smiled, a tear rolling down her cheek. "Okay, Mei. Let's meet halfway. I'll let you go, but you have to promise to be safe and happy." she agreed.

reading.cn: 梅在公园里，陷入沉思。她需要对她未来的学业做出一个艰难的决定。她缓慢地走着，享受着新鲜空气，希望能理清思绪。这是一个充满挑战的一周，她感到不知所措。最后，她在课文树下找到一个长凳，坐了下来。
reading.en: Mei was at the park, deep in thought. She had a difficult decision to make about her future studies. She walked slowly, enjoying the fresh air, hoping to clear her mind. It had been a challenging week, and she felt overwhelmed. Finally, she found an empty bench under a big oak tree and sat down.

Hardly had she sat down when the answer came to her. It was so clear, so simple! She smiled, a wave of relief washing over her. All the worry from the past few days seemed to disappear. She took out her phone and quickly typed a message to her host mother, sharing her decision. The park, which had been a place of 고민 for her, now felt like a place of new beginnings. She stood up, feeling lighter and more determined than ever. Sometimes, the best answers appear when you least expect them.
reading.cn: 她刚坐下，答案就来了。它是如此清晰，如此简单！她笑了，一阵解脱感涌上心头。过去几天的所有担忧似乎都消失了。她拿出手机，迅速给她的寄宿妈妈发了一条信息，分享了她的决定。公园，之前对她来说是一个充满烦恼的地方，现在感觉像是一个新开始的地方。她站起来，感觉比以往任何时候都更轻松、更坚定。有时候，最好的答案会在你最意想不到的时候出现。

reading.en: Mei felt a profound sense of clarity. The path forward, once obscured, was now brightly illuminated. She took a deep breath, the scent of fresh cut grass filling her lungs. This decision, she knew, was the right one. She felt a surge of excitement for what was to come.
reading.cn: 梅感到一种深刻的清晰。前方的道路，曾经模糊不清，现在豁然开朗。她深吸一口气，新割的草的芬芳充满她的肺部。她知道，这个决定是正确的。她对即将到来的事情感到一阵兴奋。
她继续漫步，但这次是带着目的。她的目光扫视着地平线，充满了希望。世界似乎已经打开，充满了可能性。艰苦的工作还在前面，但她已经准备好了。她走的每一步都很坚定，这证明了她新获得的决心。梅已经准备好拥抱她的未来。

reading.cn: 罗斯玛丽·费尔并不算美丽。她年轻、聪明、大胆。她的生活就像一场每天都预先安排好的野餐。她有一个丈夫，一栋房子，一个孩子。每天，汽车都在等候送她进城。但有时，站在人行道上，罗斯玛丽希望自己没那么富有。因为那样，她就能享受一些小事情，比如在商店里买一个不考虑价格的小珐琅盒。
reading.en: Rosemary Fell was not exactly beautiful. She was young, brilliant, and daring. Her life was like a pre-arranged picnic every day. She had a husband, a house, and a child. Every day, the motor car waited to take her into town. But sometimes, standing on the pavement, Rosemary wished she was not quite so rich. For then, she would be able to enjoy the little things, like buying a tiny enamel box in a shop without a thought to the price.

One rainy afternoon, Rosemary was shopping in a small antique shop. She saw a tiny, exquisite enamel box. "How much is this?" she asked. The shopkeeper replied, "Twenty-eight guineas, madam." Rosemary hesitated. It was more than she expected. Just then, a young woman, shivering and poorly dressed, entered the shop. "Excuse me, could you spare a moment?" she whispered to Rosemary. "I'm terribly hungry, and I have nowhere to go."
reading.cn: 一个下雨的下午，罗斯玛丽正在一家小古董店购物。她看到一个精致小巧的珐琅盒。“这个多少钱？”她问。店主回答说：“太太，二十八几尼。”罗斯玛丽犹豫了。比她预期的要贵。就在那时，一个瑟瑟发抖、衣衫褴褛的年轻女子走进了店里。“打扰了，您能帮个忙吗？”她对罗斯玛丽低声说，“我非常饿，而且无处可去。”
一个突如其来的想法让罗斯玛丽感到高兴。“跟我回家吧，”她一时冲动地说，“你可以喝杯茶，也许还可以吃点东西。”这位名叫史密斯小姐的年轻女子显得很惊讶，但还是感激地接受了。罗斯玛丽把她自己想象成一位仁慈的女主人，分享着她的温暖和慷慨。这次意想不到的救助感觉像是一场真正宏大的冒险，偏离了她井然有序却有些无聊的生活。
reading.en: A sudden idea delighted Rosemary. "Come home with me," she said impulsively. "You shall have a cup of tea, and perhaps something to eat." The young woman, whose name was Miss Smith, looked surprised but gratefully accepted. Rosemary imagined herself as a benevolent hostess, sharing her warmth and generosity. This unexpected rescue felt like a truly grand adventure, a deviation from her perfectly ordered, somewhat boring life.

reading.en: Mei felt a heavy weight on her shoulders. The new semester had just begun, but she already felt overwhelmed. Her classes were demanding, and she was trying to get involved in student clubs. "I've been feeling overwhelmed lately," she confided in her friend, Lily, during a quiet moment in the library. "I just can't seem to manage everything." Lily listened patiently. "I understand, Mei. It's a new environment, and there's a lot to adjust to. Maybe you're trying to do too much at once?" Mei sighed. "I guess so. I want to do well in my studies and make new friends, but I feel like I'm constantly running out of time. I'm starting to feel really burnt out." Lily offered a comforting smile. "It's okay to feel that way. When I felt overwhelmed, I learned to prioritize. Maybe you can try to take a break and then re-evaluate your schedule? Remember, your well-being comes first." Mei nodded, a small sense of relief washing over her. "Thanks, Lily. I needed to hear that."
reading.cn: 梅的肩上感到沉甸甸的。新学期刚刚开始，但她已经感到力不从心。“我最近感觉压力好大，”在图书馆的一个安静时刻，她向朋友莉莉倾诉。“我好像什么都应付不过来了。”莉莉耐心听着。“我明白，梅。这是一个新环境，有很多需要适应的地方。也许你正在尝试一次做太多事情？”梅叹了口气。“我想是吧。我想好好学习，交新朋友，但我觉得自己时间总是不够用。我开始感到筋疲力尽。”莉莉给了她一个安慰的微笑。“有这种感觉没关系。当我感到不知所措时，我学会了优先处理事情。也许你可以休息一下，然后重新评估你的时间表？记住，你的健康最重要。”梅点了点头，感到一丝轻松。“谢谢你，莉莉。我需要听到这些。”

梅决定采纳莉莉的建议。她用接下来的一个下午在公园里散步，享受新鲜空气，并写下她的感受。她意识到自己确实承担了太多的责任。好好睡了一晚后，梅感觉好了一些。她首先退出了一个学生社团，并决定花更多时间在她的核心课程上。她还在学习期间安排了短暂的休息。当她再次见到莉莉时，她的表情明亮了许多。“休息一下真的让我的头脑清醒了。我现在仍然很忙，但感觉更能掌控一切了。谢谢你帮我认识到我不需要做到完美。”莉莉笑了笑。“当然，梅。我们都有那些时刻。重要的是要倾听自己的声音，并在需要时寻求帮助。”
reading.en: Mei decided to take Lily's advice. She spent the next afternoon walking in the park, enjoying the fresh air, and writing down her feelings. She realized that she had indeed taken on too many responsibilities. After a good night's sleep, Mei felt a little better. She started by cutting back on one of the student clubs and decided to spend more time on her core classes. She also planned small breaks throughout her study sessions. When she saw Lily again, she had a brighter expression. "Taking a break really helped clear my head. I'm still busy, but I feel much more in control now. Thanks for helping me realize I don't have to be perfect." Lily smiled. "Of course, Mei. We all have those moments. The important thing is to listen to yourself and ask for help when you need it."

reading.cn: 梅的经历教会了她宝贵的一课：感到不适是正常的，寻求支持就更好了。她明白了自我关怀并非自私；它对长期的成功和幸福至关重要。从那时起，每当她开始感到不知所措时，她都会记住停下来，反思，并调整。她还特意与朋友保持联系，因为她知道分担的负担会更轻。
reading.en: Mei's experience taught her a valuable lesson: it's okay to not be okay, and it's even better to seek support. She learned that self-care isn't selfish; it's essential for long-term success and well-being. From then on, whenever she started feeling overwhelmed, she would remember to pause, reflect, and adjust. She also made a point to check in with her friends, knowing that shared burdens are lighter.

The next time you're feeling overwhelmed, remember Mei's story. Take a deep breath, acknowledge your feelings, and consider what small steps you can take to ease the pressure. Whether it's taking a break, asking for help, or re-prioritizing your tasks, remember that your well-being should always come first. You're not alone in this, and it's always okay to take care of yourself.
reading.cn: 下次当你感到不知所措时，记住梅的故事。深呼吸，承认你的感受，并考虑你可以采取哪些小步骤来缓解压力。无论是休息一下，寻求帮助，还是重新安排任务的优先级，请记住你的健康永远是第一位的。你不是一个人在战斗，照顾好自己总是没错的。

listening.audio: Priya found Mei sitting alone in her room, tears silently streaming down her face. Mei had just received terrible news from home, and her world felt like it was falling apart. She was heartbroken and couldn't stop crying. Priya didn't say much at first. She just sat next to Mei, offering a quiet, comforting presence. After a while, Mei looked up, her eyes red and swollen. "It's just… so much to handle," Mei whispered. Priya gently put an arm around her. "I'm so sorry you're going through this, Mei. Remember what I always say? Real friends show up when it matters. I'm here for you, whatever you need." Mei leaned into Priya, finding warmth and support. "Thank you, Priya. It means a lot to know you're here." Priya just held her, letting Mei cry until she felt a little better. Sometimes, just having a friend by your side is all the comfort you need.

grammar.explain:
'Should' 用于表达建议、责任或预期。'Shouldn't' 是 'should not' 的缩写，用于表达不建议做的事情或不应该发生的事情。 

核心用法：

*   **建议或义务：** 你应该做某事 (You should do something.)
*   **不建议或不应该：** 你不应该做某事 (You shouldn't do something.)
*   **预期（较少见在此级别）：** 某事应该发生 (Something should happen.)

reading.en: It was late October, and Mei was feeling tired. She had been working hard, studying for her English classes, and helping with chores at her host family's home. Every morning she woke up early and her days were full. She often felt a little dizzy.
reading.cn: 十月下旬，梅感到很疲惫。她一直在努力工作，学习英语课程，并且帮寄宿家庭做家务。她每天早上很早起床，日子过得很充实。她常常感到有点头晕。
梅坐下来，拿起日记本，思考着过去几周。“我总是很忙，”她写道，“休息不是奢侈品。它是必需品，尤其是我在学习一门新语言和生活在一个新文化中时。我不应该因为休息而感到内疚。”
reading.en: Mei sat down with her journal, thinking about her past few weeks. "I'm always busy," she wrote. "Rest isn't a luxury. It's a necessity, especially when I'm studying a new language and living in a new culture. I shouldn't feel guilty about taking a break."

She realized she was feeling overwhelmed and close to burnout. Mei decided to make a change. She made a new schedule that included specific times for relaxation. She talked to her host mother, Mrs. Smith, about her feelings, and Mrs. Smith was very understanding. "Mei, you're right. Everyone needs time to recharge," Mrs. Smith said.
reading.cn: 她意识到自己感到不知所措，快要精疲力尽了。梅决定做出改变。她制定了一个新的日程表，其中包括具体的放松时间。她和她的寄宿妈妈史密斯夫人谈了她的感受，史密斯夫人非常理解。“梅，你说得对。每个人都需要时间来充电，”史密斯夫人说。
从那时起，梅开始多休息。她会读一本书，听音乐，或者只是安静地坐一会儿。她注意到有很大的不同。她感觉更有活力，更专注了。她的英语学习甚至也进步了，因为她不再总是那么疲惫。梅明白照顾好自己和努力工作一样重要。
reading.en: From then on, Mei started taking more breaks. She would read a book, listen to music, or just sit quietly for a while. She noticed a big difference. She felt more energetic and focused. Her English studies even improved because she wasn't so tired all the time. Mei learned that taking care of herself was just as important as working hard.

grammar.explain: 在口语和书面语中，'can' 和 'may' 都可以用来提出建议或表达可能性。它们在含义上略有不同，'may' 通常表示更大的不确定性或更礼貌的建议。在本课场景中，Mrs. Davis 用 'may' 给出建议，语气更柔和。

grammar.explain: 动名词（-ing 形式）可以作句子的主语，表示一个动作或行为。它通常被视为单数。
grammar.title: 动名词作主语
形容词后接不定式 'to do'

examples.en: I'm so sorry you're feeling this way.

examples.en: It's tough when you put in so much effort.

grammar.explain: 有些形容词可以后接不定式（to + 动词原形），用来解释为什么会有某种感受或状态。常用于表达情感或评价。

reading.cn: 梅收到了她的第一篇论文，结果不及格。她首先感到一阵失望，然后是那种不知所措的感觉。她盯着页眉上的“F”，心沉了下去。
reading.en: Mei received her first paper back, and it wasn't a pass. She felt a wave of disappointment, followed by a sense of being overwhelmed. She stared at the 'F' on the top of the page, her heart sinking.
Later that day, Mei talked to her host mother, Mrs. Davis. "I feel so stressed about this," Mei confessed, tears welling up in her eyes. "I studied so hard, but it wasn't enough."
reading.cn: 那天晚些时候，梅和她的寄宿妈妈戴维斯太太交谈。梅坦白道：“我对此感到压力很大。”眼泪涌上她的眼眶。“我学习得很努力，但还是不够。”

reading.en: Mrs. Davis listened patiently. "Oh, Mei, I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. It's tough when you put in so much effort," she said gently. "But remember, your mental health deserves the same care as your physical health. Getting a bad grade is disappointing, but it's not the end of the world."
reading.cn: 戴维斯太太耐心地倾听着。她轻声说：“哦，梅，你这样我很难过。当你付出这么多努力时，这确实很难。”“但请记住，你的心理健康值得和你的身体健康一样的关心。成绩不好固然令人失望，但这不是世界末日。”
戴维斯太太继续说道：“也许你可以和你的教授谈谈，或者去学术支持中心。他们可以提供资源帮助你进步。最重要的是，花些时间给自己。不要让这个一次的成绩定义你。”
reading.en: Mrs. Davis continued, "Maybe you can talk to your professor, or visit the academic support center. They can provide resources to help you improve. And most importantly, take some time for yourself. Don't let this one grade define you."

reading.cn: 谈话后，梅感觉好了一些。戴维斯太太的话提醒她，有时候，不舒服也没关系，寻求帮助是坚强的表现。
reading.en: Mei felt a little better after the conversation. Mrs. Davis's words reminded her that sometimes, it's okay to not be okay, and that seeking help is a sign of strength.

output.sample: I've been using a fitness tracker for about a year now. It helps me monitor my daily steps and sleep patterns. Initially, I just wanted to track my activity, but it also sends me reminders to stand up and move if I've been sitting too long. I think technology truly shapes how we live, especially regarding health prevention. My tracker once alerted me to a slightly elevated heart rate during a stressful period, which made me pay more attention to my stress levels. This early detection was really helpful. I believe these wearable devices can be powerful tools for personal health management, helping us understand our bodies better and adopt healthier lifestyles.

reading.cn: 琳达平时不太关注自己的健康。她大部分时间都感觉良好。但最近，她做了年度体检。结果显示一个小问题：心律不齐，也称为心律失常。医生说：“这不严重，但我们需要监测。科技塑造了我们的生活方式，尤其是在现在的医疗保健领域。现在有很多新方法可以追踪你的健康状况。”琳达有点担心，但也很好奇。
reading.en: Linda usually doesn't pay much attention to her health. She feels fine most of the time. But recently, she had her annual medical check-up. The results showed a minor issue: an irregular heartbeat, also known as arrhythmia. The doctor said, "It's not severe, but we need to monitor it. Technology shapes how we live, especially in healthcare now. There are many new ways to track your health." Linda was a bit worried but also curious.

The doctor recommended a wearable device to monitor her heart rhythm daily. "This watch can collect data on your heart rate and alert you if there's anything unusual," the doctor explained. "It's a great example of how technology allows for early detection and prevention." Linda thought about it. She realized that technology could indeed help her manage her health better. She decided to try the wearable device. She hoped it would help her understand her body and keep her healthy.
reading.cn: 医生推荐了一个可穿戴设备来日常监测她的心律。医生解释说：“这款手表可以收集你的心率数据，并在有异常情况时提醒你。这是科技如何实现早期检测和预防的一个很好的例子。”琳达思考了一下。她意识到科技确实可以帮助她更好地管理自己的健康。她决定尝试可穿戴设备。她希望它能帮助她了解自己的身体并保持健康。
几周后，琳达开始使用可穿戴设备。它记录了她的心率和活动水平。她可以在手机上看到实时数据。有一天，手表发出警报：心率异常。
reading.en: A few weeks later, Linda began to use the wearable device. It recorded her heart rate and activity levels. She could see real-time data on her phone. One day, the watch sent an alert:

reading.cn: 医生证实，这个智能手表帮助发现了原本可能被忽略的细微变化。“看，科技塑造了我们的生活方式，并延伸到我们管理健康的方式。这种早期检测非常重要。”医生说。琳达松了一口气，心存感激。她明白科技不仅仅是娱乐；它也是个人健康管理的一个强大工具。
reading.en: The doctor confirmed that the watch helped catch a subtle change that might have been missed otherwise. "See, technology shapes how we live and extends to how we manage our health. This early detection is very important," the doctor stated. Linda was relieved and grateful. She learned that technology is not just about entertainment; it's also a powerful tool for personal health management.

reading.cn: 那是一个安静的周二晚上。我正坐在书桌前，全神贯注地复习历史考试。房子里很安静，只有我笔记本电脑的轻微嗡嗡声。突然，我的手机在桌上大声震动起来。是我妈妈打来的。
reading.en: It was a quiet Tuesday evening. I was sitting at my desk, deep in revision for my history exam. The house was still, except for the gentle hum of my laptop. Suddenly, my phone buzzed loudly on the table. It was my mom.

reading.cn: 我拿起电话，以为她会提醒我一些琐碎的事情。但她的声音都在颤抖。“我学习的时候，消息传开了，”她开头说，“奶奶中风了。”我心头一沉。我简直不敢相信我听到的一切。
reading.en: I picked it up, expecting her to remind me about something trivial. But her voice was shaky. "The news broke while I was studying," she began, "Grandma had a stroke." My heart dropped. I couldn't believe what I was hearing.

"Is she okay? Is she conscious?" I asked, my own voice trembling. Mom said, "She's in the hospital. The doctors are taking care of her. We're waiting for an update." I felt a mix of shock and worry. My grandma is usually so strong and healthy.
reading.cn: “她还好吗？她清醒吗？”我问，我的声音也颤抖起来。妈妈说：“她在医院。医生正在照顾她。我们正在等最新的消息。”我感到震惊和担忧交织在一起。我奶奶平时总是那么坚强和健康。

reading.en: I immediately packed a small bag and headed to the hospital. When I saw her, she was pale but trying to smile. It was a huge relief to see her conscious, even though she was still weak. I stayed by her side, holding her hand, for a long time that night.
reading.cn: 我立刻收拾了一个小包，赶往医院。当我看到她时，她脸色苍白，但努力想微笑。看到她清醒过来，真是个巨大的解脱，尽管她还是很虚弱。那天晚上我一直守在她身边，紧握着她的手，很久。

listening.audio: It was a quiet Tuesday evening. I was sitting at my desk, deep in revision for my history exam. The house was still, except for the gentle hum of my laptop. Suddenly, my phone buzzed loudly on the table. It was my mom. I picked it up, expecting her to remind me about something trivial. But her voice was shaky. "The news broke while I was studying," she began, "Grandma had a stroke." My heart dropped. I couldn't believe what I was hearing. "Is she okay? Is she conscious?" I asked, my own voice trembling. Mom said, "She's in the hospital. The doctors are taking care of her. We're waiting for an update." I felt a mix of shock and worry. My grandma is usually so strong and healthy. I immediately packed a small bag and headed to the hospital. When I saw her, she was pale but trying to smile. It was a huge relief to see her conscious, even though she was still weak. I stayed by her side, holding her hand, for a long time that night.

reading.cn: 梅在北京的医院病床边，握着奶奶虚弱的手。奶奶看起来很安详，但梅感到一阵悲伤。她想起多年前搬到国外，对新生活充满兴奋。那时候，打电话很贵，时差也很麻烦。“要是当时知道每一刻有多么宝贵，我就会更经常打电话了，”她低声说。“早知道我就多打点电话了，我会珍惜每一次通话。”她闭上眼睛，想象着奶奶温暖的笑容。“我后悔没能早点回来探望。我当时真该多回来几趟的。”
reading.en: Mei sat by her grandma's hospital bed in Beijing, holding her frail hand. Grandma looked peaceful, but Mei felt a pang of sadness. She remembered moving abroad years ago, full of excitement for a new life. Back then, calls were expensive and time differences were a hassle. “If only I had known how precious every moment was, I would have called more often,” she whispered. "Had I known, I would have cherised every single conversation." She closed her eyes, picturing her grandma's warm smile. "I regret not visiting sooner. I would have made more trips back."

output.cn: 现在请回忆一下你过去的一个决定，你现在感到后悔或者希望当时能做出不同的选择。请用英文写下你当时的设想和现在的感受，并解释你为什么会有这种感受。请确保使用至少一句 “Had I known, I would have…” 或 “If only I had…” 的句型。

output.sample: Social media algorithms often promote content that generates strong emotions, including outrage, because it leads to higher engagement like likes and shares. This can make angry posts go viral quickly. As a result, people might find themselves in 'echo chambers' where they only see content that confirms their existing views and fuels their anger, which can spread misinformation and polarize society.

reading.en: Mei: Well, a lot of experts say it's because social media rewards outrage. The algorithms are designed to show us content that keeps us scrolling, and unfortunately, anger and strong emotions tend to grab attention.

reading.cn: 薇：所以，一个帖子获得的愤怒互动越多，它就会被展示给更多人吗？
reading.en: Wei: So, the more angry interactions a post gets, the more it's shown to others?

Mei: Exactly. Likes, shares, comments – even angry ones – signal to the algorithm that the content is engaging. And what happens then? It goes viral. People get stuck in these echo chambers where they only see things that fuel their anger.
reading.cn: 梅：没错。点赞、分享、评论——即使是愤怒的——都会向算法发出信号，表明内容很吸引人。然后会发生什么？它就会走红。人们陷入这种回音室效应中，只看到那些助长他们愤怒的东西。

reading.cn: 梅一直相信教育不止于教室。在国外的新生活安顿下来后，她决定付诸行动，成为一名私人教师。她专攻英语，帮助当地那些在语言学习上遇到困难的高中生。
reading.en: Mei has always believed that education extends beyond the classroom. After settling into her new life abroad, she decided to put this belief into action by becoming a private tutor. She specializes in English, helping local high school students who struggle with the language.

reading.cn: 她的第一个学生汤姆，觉得写作文很头疼。梅不只教他语法规则；她鼓励他阅读英文小说，看美剧，并就他喜欢的话题和她练习口语。她希望他不仅仅把英语看作一门学校科目，而是一个探索世界的工具。
reading.en: Her first student, Tom, found essays challenging. Mei didn't just teach him grammar rules; she encouraged him to read English novels, watch American TV shows, and practice speaking with her about his favorite topics. She wanted him to see English not just as a school subject but as a tool for exploring the world.

reading.cn: 梅还向汤姆介绍了在线学习资源和语言交换应用程序，教他如何利用科技优势。她教导他学习是一个持续的过程，每天、每时每刻都在发生。汤姆的成绩显著提高，更重要的是，他对英语产生了真正的热爱。梅感到很自豪，她意识到自己不只是在教一门课；她是在启发一个学习者。
reading.en: Mei also introduced Tom to online learning resources and language exchange apps, showing him how to use technology to his advantage. She taught him that learning is a continuous process, happening every day, everywhere. Tom's grades improved significantly, but more importantly, he developed a genuine love for English. Mei felt proud, realizing she wasn't just teaching a subject; she was inspiring a learner.

listening.audio: Have you ever thought about the magic of small habits? It's like compound interest, but for your life. Imagine you want to read more. Instead of trying to read a whole book in one go, start with just one page a day. It seems like a tiny step, right? But if you are consistent, that one page a day will compound. In a month, you've read about 30 pages. In a year, over 365 pages – that's often more than one book! The magic isn't in the size of the habit, but in its consistency and the power of compounding. This principle applies to everything: learning a new language, getting fit, or even saving money. Don't underestimate the power of starting small. Sustainable habits are built not on grand gestures, but on consistent, tiny actions that compound over time, creating incredible momentum. So, what small habit can you start today that will compound into something great tomorrow?

reading.cn: 你有没有想过小习惯的魔力？它就像复利，但作用于你的生活。假设你想多读书。与其一口气读完一整本书，不如从每天一页开始。这看起来是很小的一步，对吗？
reading.en: Have you ever thought about the magic of small habits? It's like compound interest, but for your life. Imagine you want to read more. Instead of trying to read a whole book in one go, start with just one page a day. It seems like a tiny step, right?

reading.cn: 但如果你坚持不懈，每天一页就会积累起来。一个月后，你读了大约30页。一年后，超过365页——那通常不止一本书！魔力不在于习惯的大小，而在于它的连贯性和复利的力量。
reading.en: But if you are consistent, that one page a day will compound. In a month, you've read about 30 pages. In a year, over 365 pages – that's often more than one book! The magic isn't in the size of the habit, but in its consistency and the power of compounding.

reading.cn: 这个原则适用于一切：学习一门新语言，健身，甚至是存钱。不要低估从小处着手的力量。可持续的习惯不是建立在宏伟的姿态上，而是建立在随着时间积累的、持续的、微小的行动上，从而产生惊人的势头。

listening.audio: Mei and her dad had been arguing earlier about her mom's treatment plan. Mei felt strongly about one option, and her dad was equally firm about another. But now, seeing how worried her dad looked, Mei knew it was time to stop. “Dad, I know we disagree, but there's no use arguing anymore. Mom needs us to be strong, not fighting.” Her dad looked at her, his eyes red-rimmed and tired. “You're right, Mei. You're absolutely right. I'm just so exhausted and worried.” Mei reached for his hand. “I know, Dad. We'll get through this together. No matter what happens, we're a team.” Her dad squeezed her hand, a small, grateful smile touching his lips. “A team. Yes. And perhaps we can discuss the options calmly later, when we both have clearer heads.” Mei nodded. It was a small step, but a hopeful one.

No matter what happens, we're a team.” Her dad squeezed her hand, a small, grateful smile touching his lips. “A team. Yes. And perhaps we can discuss the options calmly later, when we both have clearer heads.” Mei nodded. It was a small step, but a hopeful one.

grammar.explain: 混合条件句用于表达与过去事实相反的假设，其结果却影响到现在。通常用于表达后悔或设想。

examples.cn: 我真希望去年夏天回来看过她。(言下之意：我没去看，现在很后悔。)

如果我那时花更多的时间陪她，也许我现在就不会有这种沉重的负罪感了。(过去条件，现在结果)
examples.en: If I had spent more time with her back then, maybe I wouldn't feel this heavy sense of guilt now. (Past condition, present result)
