grammar.title: “I wish I'd + 过去分词”表达对过去的遗憾
grammar.explain: 当我们希望过去的事情与实际发生的不同，并对此感到遗憾时，可以使用“I wish I'd + 过去分词”的结构。

examples.cn: 如果我当时探望了她，我现在会感觉好得多。(但我没去，所以现在感觉很糟糕。)
examples.en: If I had visited her, I would be feeling much better now. (But I didn't visit, so I feel bad now.)
If he had taken that job, he would be living in New York now. (But he didn't take the job, so he isn't living in New York.)
examples.cn: 如果他接受了那份工作，他现在就会住在纽约了。(但他没接受，所以他没住在纽约。)

examples.en: If she had saved money, she wouldn't be in debt today. (But she didn't save, so she is in debt.)
examples.cn: 如果她当时存了钱，她今天就不会负债了。(但她没存，所以她负债了。)

grammar.title: If I had + 过去分词..., I would + (现在时动词). (过去条件，现在结果)
grammar.explain: 这种混合条件句表达的是，如果过去的某个条件满足了，那么现在的结果就会不同。

reading.en: Mei stood in the quiet hospital corridor, the subtle scent of disinfectant hanging in the air. Her grandmother had been unwell for some time, but Mei had been so caught up with her new job and settling into her host family's home last summer. Now, looking at the closed door of her grandmother's room, a wave of sadness washed over her. She thought about the video calls, the quick chats, but never a real visit. A deep sigh escaped her lips as she whispered to herself.
reading.cn: 梅站在安静的医院走廊里，空气中弥漫着淡淡的消毒水味。她的奶奶已经不舒服一段时间了，但去年夏天梅忙于新工作和适应寄宿家庭的生活。现在，看着奶奶病房紧闭的门，一阵悲伤涌上心头。她想到了视频通话，快速的聊天，但从未真正探望过。她叹了口气，对自己低声说道。

reading.en: “I wish I’d visited her last summer. I really do. If I had known she would get so sick, I would have made time, even if it meant sacrificing a weekend. Now, I regret not prioritizing her visit. If I had spent more time with her back then, maybe I wouldn't feel this heavy sense of guilt now. I keep wondering, 'What if I had just taken that one trip?'” Mei's eyes welled up. The 'what if' echoed in the silent hall, a painful reminder of missed chances and the heavy weight of regret.
reading.cn: “我真希望去年夏天回来看过她。真的。如果我知道她会病得这么重，我当时一定会抽出时间，即使这意味着牺牲一个周末。现在，我后悔没有把探望她放在首位。如果我那时花更多的时间陪她，也许我现在就不会有这种沉重的负罪感。我一直在想，‘如果我当时去了那一趟旅行会怎么样？’”梅的眼睛湿润了。“要是当初”在寂静的走廊里回响，痛苦地提醒着她错过的机会和沉重的悔意。
一位护士走过，投来同情的目光。梅深吸一口气，努力让自己平静下来。她知道后悔过去无法改变现在，但这种感觉是压倒性的。这是一个关于在为时已晚之前，为重要的人腾出时间的沉重教训。
reading.en: A nurse walked by, offering a sympathetic glance. Mei took a deep breath, trying to compose herself. She knew regretting the past wouldn't change the present, but the feeling was overwhelming. It was a tough lesson learned about making time for the people who matter, before it's too late.
Mei thought, "If I had visited her, I would be feeling much better now." This thought brought a fresh wave of sadness. It was a past action that, if changed, would have a different present outcome.

grammar.title: 混合条件句 (Mixed Conditionals)
grammar.explain: 混合条件句结合了不同时态的条件句。常见的形式是：如果过去发生了某事（与过去事实相反的假设），那么现在会是何种情况（对现在情况的假设）。

reading.cn: 梅在寄宿家庭的头几周既令人兴奋又精疲力尽。她努力吸收一切：新语言、文化、学业挑战。她的寄宿妈妈戴维斯夫人注意到梅常常熬夜。
reading.en: Mei found her first few weeks in the host family exhilarating but exhausting. She was trying to absorb everything: the new language, the culture, the academic challenges. Her host mother, Mrs. Davis, noticed Mei burning the midnight oil.

reading.cn: “梅，你看起来很累，”戴维斯夫人一天早上温柔地说。“你睡够了吗？”
reading.en: "Mei, you look tired," Mrs. Davis said gently one morning. "Are you getting enough sleep?"

reading.cn: 梅叹了口气。“我想学好，戴维斯夫人。我学习得越多，就越觉得能学到更多。这就像复利，对吗？我现在投入的精力越多，以后受益就越大。”
reading.en: Mei sighed. "I want to do well, Mrs. Davis. The more I study, the more I feel I can learn. It's like compound interest, right? The more effort I put in now, the more I'll benefit later."

reading.cn: 戴维斯夫人笑了。“你说得对，梅。但记住，即使是复利也需要健康的本金才能增长。你的身体和Minds是你的本金。过度劳累实际上会降低你的工作效率和学习质量。这样想吧：你休息得越多，你做得就越好。”
reading.en: Mrs. Davis smiled. "That's a good point, Mei. But remember, even compound interest needs a healthy principal to grow. Your body and mind are your principal. Overworking can actually decrease your productivity and the quality of your learning. Think of it this way: The more you rest, the better you do."

reading.cn: 梅停下来，思考着。“所以，我的学习理念可能需要把休息也作为投资的一部分？”
reading.en: Mei paused, considering. "So, my philosophy about studying might need to include resting as part of the investment?"

reading.cn: 戴维斯夫人点点头。“没错。充分休息的头脑学得更高效，精力充沛的身体有更多能量。这是一种实现目标的可持续方法。你压力越小，就越能享受在这里的经历。”
reading.en: Mrs. Davis nodded. "Exactly. A well-rested mind learns more effectively, and a refreshed body has more energy. It's a sustainable way to achieve your goals. The less stressed you are, the more you can enjoy your experience here."

reading.cn: 梅把戴维斯夫人的建议铭记在心。她开始进行短暂休息，确保充足睡眠，并安排一些放松时间。令她惊讶的是，她不仅感觉好多了，学习表现也更好了。她意识到休息的“复利”确实起到了作用。
reading.en: Mei took Mrs. Davis's advice to heart. She started taking short breaks, ensuring she had enough sleep, and scheduling some time for relaxation. To her surprise, she not only felt better but also performed better in her studies. She realized that the "compound interest" of rest truly made a difference.

output.sample: In my experience, "The more I rest, the better I do" is absolutely true. During college, I used to pull all-nighters before exams, thinking that more study time meant better grades. However, I often felt exhausted and couldn't focus during the actual exam. My mind was foggy, and I made silly mistakes. Later, I changed my approach. I made sure to get at least 7-8 hours of sleep before big exams and scheduled short breaks during study sessions. To my surprise, I felt much more alert, my memory improved, and I could recall information more easily. Even with fewer "study hours" logged, the quality of my learning and my performance significantly improved. It taught me that a well-rested mind is the best tool for effective learning and problem-solving.

output.sample:
Entry: April 25th

It's hard to believe how fast time flies. This spring has been a whirlwind of new experiences, and I'm so grateful for every moment. As I look ahead to the next year, I'm starting to think about where I might be. 

I'm not entirely sure where I'll end up—maybe I'll stay in this city, or perhaps I’ll explore a new country. The possibilities are endless, and that's both exciting and a little daunting. 

Regardless of where I end up, I know I want to keep learning and growing. I want to embrace new challenges, meet interesting people, and continue to step out of my comfort zone. I hope to carry with me the openness and curiosity I’ve found this spring. I want to cherish every new experience and build a life that feels authentic to me, no matter the location. The journey itself is what matters most.

reading.cn: “三年前的今天，她的丈夫和两个年轻的兄弟就是从那扇窗户出去打猎的，”维拉说，“他们再也没回来。他们的尸体从未被找到。那扇窗户每晚都开着，直到天黑，以防他们回来。”
reading.en: “Through that window, three years ago to a day, her husband and her two young brothers went off for their day’s shooting,” said Vera, “and they never came back. Their bodies were never recovered. And the window is kept open every evening until dark, in case they should return.”

reading.cn: 弗拉姆顿听得越来越害怕。突然，萨普尔顿夫人走了进来，愉快地说她的丈夫和兄弟们会很快从那扇窗户回来。弗拉姆顿看着维拉，维拉则平静地看着窗户。
reading.en: Framton listened with growing horror. Suddenly, Mrs. Sappleton entered and cheerfully spoke of her husband and brothers returning soon through that very window. Framton looked at Vera, who calmly watched the window.

reading.cn: 就在那时，三个人影穿过草坪，走向窗户。弗拉姆顿看到“鬼魂”，抓起帽子和手杖，以最快的速度跑了出去。萨普尔顿夫人很困惑。“他看到了那只长耳猎犬，以为是鬼！”维拉说。
reading.en: Just then, three figures walked across the lawn towards the window. Framton, seeing ghosts, grabbed his hat and stick and ran out as fast as he could. Mrs. Sappleton was confused. “He saw the spaniel and thought it was a ghost!” Vera said.

listening.audio: Framton Nuttel was visiting the Sappletons. He hoped the quiet country life would calm his nerves. Mrs. Sappleton was not in the room yet, so his niece, Vera, entertained him. Vera pointed to a large French window that was open. “Through that window, three years ago to a day, her husband and her two young brothers went off for their day’s shooting,” said Vera, “and they never came back. Their bodies were never recovered. And the window is kept open every evening until dark, in case they should return.” Framton listened with growing horror. Suddenly, Mrs. Sappleton entered and cheerfully spoke of her husband and brothers returning soon through that very window. Framton looked at Vera, who calmly watched the window. Just then, three figures walked across the lawn towards the window. Framton, seeing ghosts, grabbed his hat and stick and ran out as fast as he could. Mrs. Sappleton was confused. “He saw the spaniel and thought it was a ghost!” Vera said.

output.sample: I found the ending of "The Open Window" to be incredibly shocking and darkly humorous. The very strangest part for me was Vera's final comment: "He saw the spaniel and thought it was a ghost!" This instantly made me question whatever else she had said throughout the conversation. It shows her incredible cunning and manipulative nature. I was completely fooled by her story, which made the twist even more impactful. It made me realize that Vera was by far the best storyteller in the room, even if her stories weren't true. It's a story that truly makes you question whoever you are talking to.

grammar.title: -ever 的用法

examples.cn: 无论谁告诉你窗户总是开着，他都是对的。(强调：任何人)

reading.en: Mei had been working as an intern at a marketing company for three months. She was nearing the end of her internship and felt incredibly grateful for the experience and her supervisor's support. One afternoon, she walked into her supervisor, Mr. Harrison's, office.
reading.cn: 梅在一家营销公司实习了三个月，实习期即将结束。她对这次经历和主管的支持感到非常感激。一天下午，她走进主管哈里森先生的办公室。

reading.en: Mei: "Mr. Harrison, do you have a moment?"
reading.cn: 梅：“哈里森先生，您有空吗？”

reading.en: Mr. Harrison: "Yes, Mei, come on in. What's up?"
reading.cn: 哈里森先生：“有，梅，进来吧。有什么事？”
梅：“我只是想再次感谢您所作的一切。我的实习期快结束了，我学到了很多。我真的很感谢您对我的耐心，尤其是我刚开始的时候，觉得有些任务很复杂。 ”
reading.en: Mei: "I just wanted to say thank you again for everything. My internship is almost over, and I've learned so much. I do appreciate your patience with me, especially when I was just starting and found some tasks quite complex."
Mr. Harrison: "Of course, Mei. You've been a great intern. It's natural to find things challenging at first. You've shown a lot of progress and a willingness to learn."
reading.cn: 哈里森先生：“当然了，梅。你是个很棒的实习生。刚开始觉得有挑战是正常的。你进步很大，也表现出了很强的学习意愿。”

grammar.explain: 在肯定句中，我们通常不说 "I do like coffee"，而是 "I like coffee"。但加上 "do" (一般现在时) 或 "did" (一般过去时) 可以对动词进行强调，表示“确实”、“的确”或“真的”。这常见于表达强烈的情感、纠正误解或表示对比。

listening.audio: Mei received an offer to be a research assistant. Her host mother said, "Congratulations are in order! I knew you could do it." Mei was very excited about the news. They decided to celebrate her success tonight.

reading.cn: 那是一个漆黑的秋夜。一位老银行家正在回忆很久以前的一次聚会。许多聪明的人出席了，他们讨论着无期徒刑和死刑。人们争论着哪个更道德。
reading.en: It was a dark autumn night. An old banker was thinking about a party he had long ago. Many smart people were there, and they talked about life imprisonment and the death penalty. People debated which was more moral.

reading.cn: 银行家认为无期徒刑比死刑更人道。但一位年轻的律师不同意。
reading.en: The banker argued that life imprisonment was more humane than the death penalty. But a young lawyer disagreed.

reading.cn: “两者都是错的，”律师说，“但如果我必须选择，我宁愿面对无期徒刑，也不愿面对死亡。”
reading.en: “Both are wrong,” said the lawyer. “But if I had to choose, I would rather face life imprisonment than death.”
This led to a big bet. The banker bet two million rubles that the lawyer could not stay in solitary confinement for fifteen years. The lawyer accepted the bet.
reading.cn: 这导致了一个大赌注。银行家打赌两百万卢布，赌律师无法在单独监禁中待十五年。律师接受了赌注。
十五年来，律师独自住在银行家花园里的小屋里。他读书、弹钢琴、学习语言、写作。他学到了很多。
reading.en: For fifteen years, the lawyer lived alone in a lodge in the banker’s garden. He read books, played the piano, studied languages, and wrote. He learned a lot.

output.cn: 请结合课文内容，思考律师的人生选择，并用英语表达你的看法。例如，他获得了什么？失去了什么？
output.sample: I think the lawyer's fifteen years of solitude for the bet was worth it in some ways, but not in others. He gained immense knowledge and wisdom from reading and studying, which allowed him to understand the world differently. This experience transformed him from a materialistic young man to someone who despised worldly wealth. However, he lost fifteen valuable years of his youth and social interaction. While he gained intellectual wealth, he sacrificed human connection and direct experience of life outside his confinement. Perhaps true wisdom also encompasses the understanding of human relationships and the complexities of society, which he missed during his isolation. So, while he gained a lot, I wouldn't say it was entirely worth it.
output.prompt: 你认为律师为赌约而选择的十五年独处生活是值得的吗？为什么？请用英文写一段话，阐述你的观点。

grammar.title: 强调句型: It is/was... that...
grammar.explain: “It is/was... that...” 句型用来强调句子中的某个部分，如主语、宾语或时间状语。被强调的部分放在 is/was 后面，that 引导的从句则包含句子剩余的部分。

grammar.title: 高级连接词: Though/Although/Even though

listening.audio: Mary Maloney was six months pregnant. She was a happy woman, well-pleased with her husband, Patrick. He was a detective. One evening, Patrick came home and drank a large whiskey. He told Mary something that shocked her. She couldn't believe what she heard. Mary went to the cellar to get a leg of lamb for dinner. In a daze, she came back upstairs. Patrick was standing with his back to her, looking out the window. Without thinking, Mary hit him on the back of the head with the frozen lamb. He fell to the floor, dead. Mary quickly thought about what to do. She put the lamb in the oven. Then she went to the store, pretending to be normal. When she came back, she called the police. "My husband is dead!" she cried. Detectives arrived. They searched the house but found no murder weapon. Mary offered them the cooked lamb. "You gentlemen must be hungry," she said. The police ate the evidence, discussing how mysterious the case was. Mary Maloney smiled.

grammar.title: 强调句：It was ... that/who...
grammar.explain: 强调句用来突出句子中的某个部分，如主语、宾语或状语。结构是“It is/was + 被强调部分 + that/who + 句子的其余部分”。that 用于强调物或人都可，who 专用于强调人。

examples.cn: 是帕特里克告诉了玛丽一些令人震惊的事情。（强调主语）
examples.en: It was Patrick who told Mary something shocking.

examples.cn: 是羊腿被玛丽当作凶器使用了。（强调宾语）
examples.en: It was a leg of lamb that Mary used as a weapon.

examples.cn: 谋杀案是在厨房里发生的。（强调地点状语）
examples.en: It was in the kitchen that the murder happened.

grammar.title: 省略表目的的介词 for
grammar.explain: 在某些口语或非正式的书面语中，表示目的的介词“for”有时可以省略，尤其是当目的非常明确时。但这并非所有情况都适用，通常限于表示“为了（做某事）”的结构，后面跟着动名词。

examples.cn: 她去地窖拿羊腿做晚餐。（原始句）
examples.en: She went to the cellar to get a leg of lamb for dinner.

examples.cn: 她去地窖拿羊腿晚餐。（省略 for，但此处 for 引导的是目的状语，省略后意思略有变化，变成 lamb dinner 这个词组）
examples.en: She went to the cellar to get a leg of lamb dinner.

examples.cn: 她去商店假装正常。（这里 for 并未省略，也不是 for dinner）
examples.en: She went to the store pretending to be normal.

grammar.title: 得体表达：委婉拒绝或提出请求
grammar.explain: 在英语交流中，尤其是情境像故事中 Mary 邀请侦探们吃饭时，即使对方是警察，为了显得礼貌和得体，也会使用一些委婉的表达方式。例如，使用情态动词 'must' 来表达一种推测性但带有关怀的建议，而不是直接命令。

examples.cn: “先生们一定饿了，”她说道。（委婉的建议，表示关怀）

reading.cn: 梅感到胃里一阵焦虑。这是她的最后一年，工作量非常大。尤其是“高等微积分”。米勒教授很出色但要求很高。即使额外学习，梅也总是落后。“我受够了这门课了，”她喝咖啡休息时对朋友丽莎嘟囔道。“我就是搞不懂那些概念。”
reading.en: Mei felt a knot of anxiety tighten in her stomach. It was her final year, and the workload was relentless. Especially "Advanced Calculus." The professor, Dr. Miller, was brilliant but demanding. Mei was constantly falling behind, even with extra study sessions. "I'm fed up with this class," she mumbled to her friend, Lisa, during a coffee break. "I just can't seem to grasp the concepts."

reading.cn: 丽莎同情地 C 点头。“我知道，梅。这真的很难。但你已经走了这么远了。不要让这门课把你打倒。也许我们今晚可以一起学习？”梅叹了口气。“我很感激，丽莎，但我太不知所措了。我甚至想过退掉这门课。”丽莎眼睛睁大了。“不可能！你快毕业了！你只需要再坚持几个月。”
reading.en: Lisa nodded sympathetically. "I know, Mei. It's really tough. But you've come so far. Don't let this one class get you down. Maybe we can study together tonight?" Mei sighed. "I appreciate it, Lisa, but I'm just so overwhelmed. I've even thought about dropping out of this course." Lisa's eyes widened. "No way! You're so close to graduating! You just need to tough it out for a few more months."

reading.cn: 梅往后靠了靠，感受着挫败感的重压。“我知道，我知道。只是……我真的厌倦了觉得自己不够聪明。”丽莎把手放在梅的胳膊上。“那不是真的，梅。你非常聪明。这门课只是个难缠的家伙。我们会一起想办法的。你不是一个人。”
reading.en: Mei leaned back, feeling the weight of her frustration. "I know, I know. It's just... I'm really fed up with feeling like I'm not smart enough." Lisa put a hand on Mei's arm. "That's not true, Mei. You're incredibly smart. This class is just a beast. We'll figure it out together. You're not alone."

reading.en: Once upon a time, there was a giant who had a beautiful garden. The children loved to play in his garden every afternoon. It was full of soft green grass and lovely flowers. There were also twelve peach trees that bloomed in spring and gave juicy fruit in autumn.
reading.cn: 从前，有一个巨人，他有一个美丽的花园。每天下午孩子们都喜欢在他的花园里玩耍。花园里长满了柔软的绿草和可爱的鲜花。还有十二棵桃树，春天开花，秋天结出多汁的果实。

reading.en: But the Giant was very selfish. One day, he came back and saw the children playing. "What are you doing here?" he cried in a loud voice. "My own garden is my own garden, and no one is allowed to play in it but myself." So, he built a high wall around it and put up a notice board: "TRESPASSERS WILL BE PROSECUTED."
reading.cn: 但巨人非常自私。有一天，他回来了，看到孩子们在玩耍。“你们在这里做什么？”他大声吼道。“我的花园就只是我的花园，除了我以外，任何人都不能在里面玩。”于是，他围着花园筑起一道高墙，并立了一块告示牌：“擅自闯入者，格杀勿论。”
可怜的孩子们无处玩耍。他们试图在路上玩耍，但路很脏很硬，他们不喜欢。他们放学后常常徘徊在高墙周围，谈论里面美丽的花园。“我们那时在那里是多么快乐啊！”他们互相说道。
reading.en: The poor children had nowhere to play. They tried to play on the road, but the road was dusty and full of hard stones, and they did not like it. They used to wander around the high wall when their lessons were over and talk about the beautiful garden inside. "How happy we were there!" they said to each other.

Then the Spring came, and all over the country there were little blossoms and little birds. Only in the garden of the Selfish Giant it was still Winter. The birds did not care to sing in it as there were no children, and the trees forgot to blossom. The Snow and the Frost danced around in the garden.
reading.cn: 春天来了，整个国家都开满了小花，飞满了小鸟。只有自私的巨人的花园里仍然是冬天。鸟儿们不愿在里面唱歌，因为没有孩子，树木也忘记了开花。雪花和霜冻在花园里翩翩起舞。

reading.en: One morning the Giant was lying awake in bed when he heard some lovely music. It was a little bird singing outside his window. "I think Spring has come at last," said the Giant. He looked out and saw a most wonderful sight. Through a little hole in the wall the children had crept in, and they were sitting in the branches of the trees. Every tree that he could see had a little child in it.
reading.cn: 一天早上，巨人躺在床上醒着，这时他听到了一些美妙的音乐。是一只小鸟在他的窗外唱歌。“我想春天终于来了，”巨人说。他向外望去，看到了一幅最奇妙的景象。孩子们通过墙上的一个小洞爬了进来，他们正坐在树枝上。他能看到的每棵树上都有一个小孩。

grammar.title: 第三人称单数动词的变化规则 (Present Simple Third Person Singular)
grammar.explain:
在一般现在时中，当主语是第三人称单数 (he, she, it, 或单数名词) 时，动词需要根据以下规则进行变化：

**1. 大多数动词加 `-s`:**
   - play → plays
   - sing → sings
   - like → likes
   - bloom → blooms
   - dance → dances

**2. 以 `s, x, ch, sh, o` 结尾的动词加 `-es`:**
   - teach → teaches
   - watch → watches
   - go → goes

**3. 以辅音字母加 `y` 结尾的动词，变 `y` 为 `i` 再加 `-es`:**
   - study → studies
   - try → tries

**4. 不规则动词:**
   - have → has

reading.cn: 梅深吸一口气。“这真是个艰难的决定， Sophie。旧金山现在是我的家，但西雅图的这份工作机会太棒了。”
reading.en: Mei sighed deeply. "That's a really tough decision, Sophie. San Francisco is home now, but this job offer in Seattle is amazing."
Sophie nodded. "I understand. Relocating is a big step. What are the pros and cons?"
reading.cn: Sophie 点点头。“我理解。搬迁是一大步。优点和缺点是什么？”
梅望着窗外。“嗯，在这里，我有我的朋友，我的日常生活，我最喜欢的咖啡店……但是西雅图的工作提供了更多的成长空间和更高的薪水。”
reading.en: Mei stared out the window. "Well, here, I have my friends, my routine, my favorite coffee shop... But the Seattle job offers a lot more growth and a higher salary."
Sophie smiled gently. "It sounds like you have a lot to think about. You don't have to decide right now."
reading.cn: Sophie 温柔地笑了笑。“听起来你有很多需要考虑的。你不必现在就决定。”
梅转向她。“你说得对。我不能仓促决定。我需要理清思路。让我考虑一晚。”
reading.en: Mei turned to her. "You're right. I can't just make a snap decision. I need to clear my head. Let me sleep on it."
Sophie squeezed her arm. "Good idea. Take your time. Whatever you choose, I'll support you."
reading.cn: Sophie 捏了捏她的手臂。“好主意。慢慢来。无论你选择什么，我都会支持你。”

output.sample: In a society that often values independence, the act of asking for help can sometimes be perceived as a sign of weakness. However, I believe that embracing vulnerability and seeking assistance is, in fact, a profound strength. When we create an environment where individuals feel empowered to reach out without fear of judgment, we foster growth, innovation, and stronger communities. This introduction will explore the societal perceptions surrounding asking for help and argue for a shift towards a culture that openly encourages mutual support.

reading.en: Imagine a world where asking for help is not seen as a weakness, but as a strength. A world where everyone feels comfortable reaching out, knowing they will be met with understanding and support.
reading.cn: 想象这样一个世界：求助不被视为弱点，而是力量。一个每个人都乐于伸出援手，并相信会得到理解和支持的世界。
这是我论文引言的前提。作为一名学生，我经常观察到同学甚至我自己，在面临学业或个人挑战时，不愿寻求帮助。为什么我们很难开口求助，尤其是在非常需要的时候？
reading.en: This is the premise of my thesis introduction. As a student, I've often observed a reluctance among peers, and even myself, to seek assistance when facing academic or personal challenges. Why do we struggle to ask for help, especially when it's much needed?

reading.cn: 我的研究探讨了阻碍个人寻求支持的心理和社会障碍。它旨在促进对这些障碍的更深入理解，并提出策略来创建一个更具支持性的环境。
reading.en: My research explores the psychological and social barriers that prevent individuals from seeking support. It aims to foster a deeper understanding of these obstacles and propose strategies to create a more supportive environment.

Ultimately, this thesis argues for a cultural shift: a shift towards a world where asking for help is not only easy but also encouraged. A world where asking is a natural part of growth and collaboration. Imagine that world.

reading.cn: 基亚韦住在夏威夷。他是一个有钱人但他想买一个瓶子。不是一个普通的瓶子，而是一个魔法瓶。这个瓶子里有一个小鬼。这个小鬼可以给你你想要的一切。
reading.en: Keawe lived on Hawaii. He was a rich man but he wanted to buy a bottle. Not an ordinary bottle, but a magic bottle. This bottle had an imp inside. This imp could give you everything you wanted.

reading.cn: 但有一个诅咒。当你买了瓶子之后，你必须以比你买它时更低的价格卖掉它。如果你带着瓶子死了，你的灵魂将在地狱里燃烧直到永恒。基亚韦以五十美元的价格买了瓶子。
reading.en: But there was a curse. When you bought the bottle, you had to sell it for a lower price than you paid. If you died with the bottle in your possession, your soul would burn in hell for eternity. Keawe bought the bottle for fifty dollars.

reading.cn: 基亚韦用小鬼建造了一座美妙的房子。他很高兴，但后来他想起了诅咒。他试图卖掉瓶子，但所有人都很害怕。最终，他以二十美元的价格把它卖给了一个绝望的老人。
reading.en: Keawe used the imp to build a wonderful house. He was happy, but then he remembered the curse. He tried to sell the bottle, but everyone was scared. Finally, he sold it to a desperate old man for twenty dollars.

reading.cn: 基亚韦后来爱上了一个美丽的女人，可可亚。他们结婚了。然而，基亚韦病得很重，医生告诉他他很快就会死去。他记起了诅咒，知道他必须把瓶子拿回来。
reading.en: Keawe later fell in love with a beautiful woman, Kokua. They got married. However, Keawe became very ill and was told he would die soon. He remembered the curse and knew he had to get the bottle back.

reading.cn: 他找到了那个老人，老人以一美元的价格把它卖回给他。基亚韦打破了诅咒，因为他以更低的价格买回了它。但现在他是拥有者，而且他快死了。可可亚偷偷地以七十五美分的价格从基亚韦那里买下了瓶子，挽救了他的灵魂。然后她试图卖掉它，但没有人愿意以低于七十五美分的价格购买。
reading.en: He found the old man, who sold it back to him for a dollar. Keawe had broken the curse because he bought it for a lower price. But now he was the owner, and he was going to die. Kokua secretly bought the bottle from Keawe for seventy-five cents, saving his soul. She then tried to sell it, but no one wanted it for less than seventy-five cents.

listening.audio: Mei sat at her desk, staring at the blank page. This was the final chapter of her book, "Ambitions of a New Era." She thought about all the conversations, the interviews, and the research that had led her here. Her mind drifted to the future. She typed: "By 2030, I will have built something truly impactful." She paused, reflecting on the weight of that statement. It wasn't just about a building or a company; it was about creating a positive change, a lasting legacy. She imagined a community center, a scholarship program, or maybe even a sustainable energy venture. "By then, I will have inspired countless individuals," she continued, her fingers flying across the keyboard. "I will have seen the fruits of my labor, not just in financial success, but in the smiles and improved lives of others." She felt a surge of energy. The future was not just a distant concept; it was a canvas waiting for her to paint. She smiled, ready to finish her chapter, knowing that her words were not just ink on paper, but a promise to herself and to the world.

She typed: "By 2030, I will have built something truly impactful." She paused, reflecting on the weight of that statement. It wasn't just about a building or a company; it was about creating a positive change, a lasting legacy. She imagined a community center, a scholarship program, or maybe even a sustainable energy venture.

The future was not just a distant concept; it was a canvas waiting for her to paint. She smiled, ready to finish her chapter, knowing that her words were not just ink on paper, but a promise to herself and to the world.

reading.cn: 梅觉得胃里一阵紧张。这是她的论文反馈会，戴维斯教授刚刚提出了一个关于她研究方法的重要问题。梅深吸一口气，准备好回应。
reading.en: Mei felt a knot in her stomach. It was her thesis feedback meeting, and Professor Davis had just raised a critical point about her methodology. Mei took a deep breath, ready to engage.

"Professor Davis, I appreciate you bringing that up," Mei began. "Let me address that concern directly. I chose this qualitative approach because it allows for a more nuanced understanding of participant experiences, which is crucial for my research question."
reading.cn: “戴维斯教授，我很感谢您提出这一点，”梅开口说。“请允许我直接回应这个问题。我选择这种定性方法是因为它能让人们对参与者的体验有更细致的理解，这对我研究问题至关重要。

reading.en: Professor Davis nodded slowly. "I see your reasoning, Mei. However, the data analysis section could benefit from more detailed justification of your coding process. Could you clarify that aspect further?"
reading.cn: 戴维斯教授缓慢地点了点头。“我明白你的理由，梅。但是，数据分析部分可以从更详细地论证你的编码过程。你能进一步澄清这方面吗？”
“当然，”梅回答道。“我一直在修改这一部分，正是为了澄清这一点。我还采纳了您之前关于文献综述的一些建议。我相信这些改动会加强论点。
reading.en: "Absolutely," Mei replied. "I've been working on a revised section to clarify exactly that. I've also incorporated some of your earlier suggestions regarding the literature review. I'm confident those changes will strengthen the argument."

The meeting continued, with Mei confidently addressing each point, clarifying her choices, and demonstrating her commitment to improving her thesis. By the end, the knot in her stomach had loosened considerably.
reading.cn: 会议继续进行，梅自信地回应每一个问题，澄清她的选择，并展示了她致力于改进论文的决心。会议结束时，她胃里的紧张感已经大大缓解了。

You: Exactly! We can allocate a small team to research its feasibility.
Colleague: Okay, let’s do that. Thanks for bringing that up, I appreciate your perspective.

reading.cn: 琳达：那是个很好的起点，汤姆。但你考虑过另一个角度吗？比如传统的广告，像广告牌或电视商业广告？
reading.en: Linda: That's a good starting point, Tom. But have you considered another angle? What about traditional advertising, like billboards or TV commercials?

reading.cn: 汤姆：嗯，我以为我们都同意数字营销是未来。传统广告很贵，而且它们的影响力很难衡量。
reading.en: Tom: Hmm, I thought we agreed that digital marketing is the future. Traditional ads are expensive and their impact is hard to measure.

reading.cn: 琳达：没错，但我们的一些目标受众可能不那么活跃在线上。结合的方法可以接触到更多的人。我们不想错过任何人。
reading.en: Linda: True, but some of our target audience might not be as active online. A combined approach could reach more people. We don't want to miss anyone.

reading.cn: 汤姆：你说得有道理。我没有从那个角度考虑过。那么，你建议哪种传统广告呢？
reading.en: Tom: You have a point. I didn't think about it from that perspective. So, what kind of traditional advertising are you suggesting?

reading.cn: 琳达：也许是一些地方电台的广告或社区报纸上的广告。只是为了扩大我们的覆盖范围。我们可以从小规模开始，看看效果。
reading.en: Linda: Maybe some local radio spots or ads in community newspapers. Just to broaden our reach. We can start small and see the results.

reading.cn: 汤姆：这听起来像是一个合理的替代方案。我们可以分配一小部分预算来测试一下。谢谢你提出这个建议，琳达。
reading.en: Tom: That sounds like a reasonable alternative. We could allocate a small portion of the budget to test it out. Thanks for bringing that up, Linda.

reading.en: Linda: No problem. It's good to explore all angles before making a final decision.

reading.en: Soapy was a hobo. Winter was coming, and he needed a warm place to stay. He wanted to go to prison on Blackwell's Island, where he would have food and a bed.

reading.en: Soapy tried to get arrested. First, he ate a big meal at a fancy restaurant and told the waiter he had no money. But the waiter just threw him out.

reading.cn: 接着，他打破了一个商店橱窗。一个警察看到了他，但警察认为索比不可能是肇事者，因为他没有逃跑。于是警察去追另一个人了。
reading.en: Then, he broke a shop window. A cop saw him, but the cop thought Soapy couldn't be the one because he wasn't running away. So the cop went after another man.

reading.cn: 索比感到绝望。他看到一把男人的伞，就拿走了。男人说那是他的。索比说:“那你为什么不叫警察呢?”但那个男人只是走开了，说他之前不小心拿走了伞，那不是他的。
reading.en: Soapy felt desperate. He saw a man's umbrella and took it. The man said it was his. Soapy said, "Well, why don't you call a cop?" But the man just walked away, saying he had taken the umbrella earlier by mistake, and it was not his.

reading.cn: 最后，索比路过一个教堂。他听到管风琴奏出的优美赞美诗。音乐触动了他的心弦。他想起了过去，决定改变自己的生活。
reading.en: Finally, Soapy walked past a church. He heard a beautiful anthem from the organ. The music touched his heart. He thought about his past and decided to change his life.

listening.audio: Soapy was a hobo. Winter was coming, and he needed a warm place to stay. He wanted to go to prison on Blackwell's Island, where he would have food and a bed. Soapy tried to get arrested. First, he ate a big meal at a fancy restaurant and told the waiter he had no money. But the waiter just threw him out. Then, he broke a shop window. A cop saw him, but the cop thought Soapy couldn't be the one because he wasn't running away. So the cop went after another man. Soapy felt desperate. He saw a man's umbrella and took it. The man said it was his. Soapy said, "Well, why don't you call a cop?" But the man just walked away, saying he had taken the umbrella earlier by mistake, and it was not his. Finally, Soapy walked past a church. He heard a beautiful anthem from the organ. The music touched his heart. He thought about his past and decided to change his life.

Determined to change his life for the better.

reading.en: David called his father, Mr. Li, who was visiting from China. "Hi Dad, how are you liking your visit so far?" David asked.
reading.cn: 大卫给从中国来访的父亲李先生打电话。“爸，您目前为止对这次来访感觉怎么样？”大卫问道。

reading.en: "It's good, son. But tell me, what's with this crazy weather we're having?" Mr. Li chuckled. "One day it's sunny and pretty warm, the next it's raining and chilly! In China, the weather is more predictable this time of year."
reading.cn: “挺好的，儿子。不过告诉我，我们这天气怎么这么奇怪？”李先生笑着说。“一天阳光明媚暖和和的，第二天就又下雨又冷！在中国，每年这个时候天气更可预测。”
“是啊，爸，您说得对。天气真是太奇怪了！对我们来说也算有点反常。昨天还又热又潮湿，今天就刮大风，感觉像冬天！”大卫回答道。
reading.en: "Yeah, Dad, you're right. It's totally crazy weather we're having! Even for us, it's a bit unusual. Yesterday was so hot and humid, and today there's a strong wind and it feels like winter!" David responded.

reading.cn: “好吧，看来我得准备各种衣服来应对不同的天气了，”李先生笑着说。“至少这样还挺有趣的！”
reading.en: "Well, I guess I'll just have to pack various clothes for different kinds of weather then," Mr. Li said, laughing. "At least it keeps things interesting!"

grammar.title: 称谓词的用法: Ms., Mrs., Mr., 和 Dr.
grammar.explain: 在英语中，称谓词 (honorifics) 是用来表示对人尊敬或身份的词。正确使用这些称谓词非常重要，尤其是在正式场合。本课我们重点回顾 Ms., Mrs., Mr., 和 Dr. 的用法。

examples.cn: 布朗先生将于早上9点到达。
examples.en: Mr. Brown will arrive at 9 AM.

examples.cn: 这是大卫·李先生。
examples.en: This is Mr. David Lee.

grammar.title: Mr. (Mister)
grammar.explain: 用于男性，无论已婚或未婚。

examples.en: Mrs. Davis is a wonderful host.
examples.cn: 戴维斯夫人是一位很棒的主人。

examples.en: Our new neighbor is Mrs. White.
examples.cn: 我们的新邻居是怀特夫人。

grammar.title: Mrs. (Mistress)
grammar.explain: 用于已婚女性。

reading.cn: 毕业典礼临近了。莎拉正在帮着最终确认嘉宾演讲者的名单。她看到屏幕上的一个名字：Emily Stevens 博士。莎拉知道 Stevens 博士一定会很棒，但她需要确认一个小细节。
reading.en: The graduation ceremony was just around the corner. Sarah was helping finalize the list of guest speakers. She looked at a name on her screen: Dr. Emily Stevens. Sarah knew Dr. Stevens would be fantastic, but she needed to confirm a small detail.

reading.cn: “打扰一下，约翰逊先生，”莎拉叫住她的主管。“抱歉打扰您，但我需要快速澄清一下关于 Stevens 博士的事情。”约翰逊先生正在忙其他准备工作，抬起头来。
reading.en: "Excuse me, Mr. Johnson," Sarah called to her supervisor. "Sorry to bother you, but I need a quick clarification about Dr. Stevens." Mr. Johnson, who was busy with other preparations, looked up.
"Yes, Sarah? What is it?" he asked, a little distracted.
reading.cn: “是的，莎拉？什么事？”他问道，有点心不在焉。
“嗯，我看到她被列为‘Emily Stevens 博士’，但为了节目单的统一性，我们通常在姓名后使用 Mr.、Ms. 或 Mrs. 作为非学术头衔。所以……让我确认一下——是 Ms. 还是 Mrs. Stevens？我只是想确保我们在介绍她时和在官方节目手册上使用正确的称谓。”莎拉解释道，举起节目单草稿。
reading.en: "Well, I see she's listed as 'Dr. Emily Stevens,' but for consistency in the program, we usually use Mr., Ms., or Mrs. for non-academic titles after their name. So... let me check — is it Ms. or Mrs. Stevens? I just want to make sure we use the correct honorific when we introduce her and on the official program booklet." Sarah explained, holding up the draft program.

reading.cn: 约翰逊先生笑了。“啊，莎拉，抓得好！艾米丽实际上是单身，所以应该是‘Ms. Stevens’。谢谢你再三确认。对于这样的活动来说，注重细节很重要！”莎拉点点头，很高兴自己问了。把小事做好体现了尊重。
reading.en: Mr. Johnson smiled. "Ah, good catch, Sarah! Emily is actually single, so it would be 'Ms. Stevens.' Thanks for double-checking. Attention to detail is important for an event like this!" Sarah nodded, glad she had asked. Getting the small things right showed respect.

output.prompt: 你正在准备一个重要的活动（例如毕业典礼、公司大会）。你需要确认一位重要嘉宾的称谓（Dr., Mr., Ms., Mrs.），以确保在正式场合中表现出适当的尊重。写一段简短的对话或邮件，询问或确认这个称谓。
output.sample:
Subject: Quick Confirmation for Speaker's Title - Dr. Eleanor Vance

Dear [Name of Coordinator/Assistant],

Hope you're having a productive week. 

I'm finalizing the program for the Annual Gala, and I just wanted to do a quick double-check on Dr. Eleanor Vance's preferred title for the program booklet. I have her listed as "Dr. Eleanor Vance," but I want to ensure we are consistent with how we introduce her on stage and in all our official materials. 

Could you please confirm if "Dr. Eleanor Vance" is the correct honorific, or if she prefers, for example, "Ms. Vance" in certain contexts?

Thanks for your quick clarification!

Best regards,
[Your Name]
Event Coordinator

grammar.title: 使用 "Let's find common ground." 表达寻求共识
grammar.explain: “Let's find common ground.” 是一种礼貌而直接的表达，用于建议双方在争论或分歧中寻找共同点，以达成一致或理解。它通常在对话中出现分歧时使用，旨在促进合作和解决问题。

examples.cn: 我们对方法有分歧，但让我们在最终目标上找到共识。
examples.en: We disagree on the method, but let's find common ground on the ultimate goal.

examples.cn: 双方都有强烈意见；是时候找到共识了。
examples.en: Both sides have strong opinions; it's time to find common ground.

examples.cn: 与其争论，不如让我们找到一个对所有人都有利共识。
examples.en: Instead of arguing, let's find common ground that benefits everyone.

examples.cn: 你能澄清一下你说的“充足资源”是什么意思吗？
examples.en: Could you clarify what you mean by "sufficient resources"?

examples.cn: 他问：“您能澄清一下项目时间线吗？”
examples.en: He asked, "Could you clarify the timeline for the project?"

examples.cn: 我需要你澄清你在这个问题上的立场。
examples.en: I need you to clarify your position on this matter.

grammar.title: 使用 "Could you clarify...?" 进行澄清
grammar.explain: “Could you clarify...?” 是一个礼貌的提问方式，用于请求对方对某个陈述、观点或信息进行更详细的解释或阐明，以消除误解。

grammar.title: 使用 "My main concern is..." 表达主要关注点
grammar.explain: “My main concern is...” 用于明确表达说话者最主要、最关注的问题或担忧。这有助于将对话焦点引导到核心问题上。

examples.cn: 我主要关注的是员工的安全。
examples.en: My main concern is the safety of the employees.

examples.cn: 她主要关注的是对当地社区的影响。
examples.en: Her main concern was the impact on the local community.

examples.cn: 我主要担心的是我们没有足够的时间。
examples.en: My main concern is that we don't have enough time.

listening.audio: Good morning, Dr. Chen. My name is Senator Davis. Thank you for being here today. I'd like to start by discussing the proposed budget for the new environmental initiative. From my perspective, the current allocation seems insufficient to achieve the stated goals. Could you clarify how you plan to address this potential funding gap? Good morning, Senator Davis. Thank you for your question. I understand your concern regarding the budget. While the initial allocation might appear modest, it is designed as seed funding. We anticipate securing additional grants and private investments in the coming months. We have a solid plan to attract these resources, which I can elaborate on if you wish. I appreciate that, Dr. Chen. My main concern is ensuring the initiative has the resources it needs to succeed, and I want to make sure we're on the same page. Let's find common ground here. Perhaps you could provide a more detailed breakdown of the expected grants and investments, along with a revised timeline for their acquisition? Certainly, Senator. I have those details ready. Our strategy includes partnerships with several key environmental foundations and a targeted outreach to impact investors. We project securing 40% of the additional funds within the first six months. I believe once you see the full picture, we will find much common ground.
